questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman presents with 8 years of severe pelvic pain that begins with her menses and resolves after a few days. She also reports pain with intercourse, and she and her partner have been unable to conceive for 2 years despite regular unprotected intercourse. Over-the-counter ibuprofen provides little relief. Pelvic examination is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: The classic triad of endometriosis is dysmenorrhea, dyspareunia, and infertility.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ectopic endometrial implants respond to cyclic hormones just like the uterine lining, building up and bleeding with each menses. This produces cyclic pelvic pain timed to menstruation, pain with intercourse, and infertility from fibrosis and pelvic adhesions around the ovaries and tubes. Poor response to NSAIDs also favors endometriosis over primary dysmenorrhea.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adenomyosis (endometrial tissue within the myometrium) presents with abnormal uterine bleeding and dysmenorrhea, but the uterus is diffusely enlarged and soft on examination, which this patient lacks.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chronic endometritis may be asymptomatic or cause abnormal uterine bleeding and pelvic pain, but it does not classically cause the cyclic triad with dyspareunia and infertility.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Endometrial hyperplasia presents with abnormal or excessive uterine bleeding rather than cyclic pain, dyspareunia, and infertility.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Endometrial polyps are usually asymptomatic or cause irregular pelvic bleeding, not cyclic menstrual pain with infertility.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman with long-standing cyclic pelvic pain undergoes laparoscopy, which reveals a markedly distorted right ovary containing a large cystic mass filled with dark brown fluid from previous hemorrhage. Biopsy of the cyst wall is most likely to show which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Crowded glands with prominent nucleoli and open chromatin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Endometrial glands and stroma resembling normal endometrium

choices.label: D
choices.text: Plasma cells scattered through the stroma

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sheets of malignant cells invading the ovarian cortex

explanation.summary: A chocolate cyst (endometrioma) is ovarian endometriosis, and endometriosis is histologically normal endometrial tissue in the wrong place.
explanation.whyCorrect: The ovary is the most common site of endometriosis. Repeated cyclic bleeding of ovarian implants creates cystic masses filled with old hemorrhagic fluid, called chocolate cysts or endometriomas. Histologically the lesion shows endometrial glands and stroma, often with an inflamed stroma, identical in appearance to eutopic endometrium.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Crowded, complex glands with cytologic atypia describe atypical endometrial hyperplasia/EIN, a lesion of the uterine lining, not an ovarian endometrioma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neutrophils infiltrating stroma and filling gland lumens are the hallmark of acute endometritis, not endometriosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Plasma cells in the stroma define chronic endometritis, not an ovarian endometriotic cyst.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Endometriosis is a benign condition; the cyst is formed by benign endometrial tissue and old blood, not malignant cells.

questions.stem: A 41-year-old woman with surgically confirmed pelvic endometriosis develops cyclic hemoptysis, and imaging identifies an endometriotic implant in the lung. Which of the following mechanisms best explains disease at this distant site?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ascending infection past the endocervical barrier

choices.label: B
choices.text: Invagination of the basal endometrial layer into the myometrium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Metaplasia of peritoneal mesothelial cells into endometrial cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Retrograde flow of menstrual blood through the fallopian tubes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Spread of endometrial cells through vascular and lymphatic channels

explanation.summary: Hematogenous and lymphatic dissemination of endometrial cells explains endometriosis at distant sites such as the lung.
explanation.whyCorrect: One theory of endometriosis proposes that endometrial cells enter the vascular and lymphatic systems, travel through the circulation, and then implant and multiply. This is the mechanism that accounts for rare implants far from the pelvis, including pulmonary endometriosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ascending infection relates to endometritis; the endocervix normally acts as a barrier to it, and infection does not create endometrial implants in the lung.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Invagination of the basal endometrium into the uterine wall is a proposed mechanism of adenomyosis, which is confined to the myometrium.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Coelomic metaplasia involves transformation of peritoneal or visceral mesothelial cells and explains pelvic disease, not implants in the lung.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Retrograde menstruation carries shed endometrium into the tubes, ovaries, and pelvic or peritoneal cavities; it does not account for spread to the thorax.

questions.stem: Researchers compare biopsy specimens of ectopic endometriotic implants with normal eutopic endometrium from the same patients. Compared with normal endometrial tissue, the implants are most likely to show overproduction of which of the following?

explanation.summary: Endometriotic tissue is not simply transplanted endometrium; it overproduces prostaglandins and cytokines.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although endometriosis looks histologically like normal endometrium, the ectopic tissue overproduces prostaglandins and cytokines, key mediators of the inflammatory response, compared with normal endometrial tissue. This overproduction contributes to the pain and inflammation of the disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: FSH and LH are pituitary gonadotropins; endometrial tissue responds to downstream ovarian hormones but does not secrete gonadotropins.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Progestins used in treatment suppress matrix metalloproteinases; the implants themselves are not characterized by overproducing MMP inhibitors.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The implants respond to ovarian hormones during the cycle; excess progesterone production is not a feature of endometriotic tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.E: PTEN is a tumor suppressor gene whose mutations are associated with atypical endometrial hyperplasia and endometrioid carcinoma, not endometriosis.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman with endometriosis begins an estrogen-progesterone combined oral contraceptive, and her cyclic pelvic pain improves markedly over the next 3 months. Which of the following is the most important mechanism of this benefit?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antagonism of GnRH receptors in the pituitary

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct inhibition of prostaglandin synthesis in implants

choices.label: C
choices.text: Downregulation of GnRH receptors by nonpulsatile stimulation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhibition of enzymes required for estrogen synthesis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inhibition of the midcycle surge of luteinizing hormone

explanation.summary: Combined oral contraceptives treat endometriosis chiefly by inhibiting the midcycle LH surge.
explanation.whyCorrect: Combined oral contraceptives act through several mechanisms, but most importantly they inhibit the midcycle LH surge. The resulting suppression of ovarian function eliminates the cyclic fluctuations of estrogen and progesterone that drive the buildup and bleeding of ectopic implants, so hormone-responsive pain improves.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blocking the GnRH receptor without an initial gonadotropin rise is the mechanism of GnRH antagonists, not combined oral contraceptives.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Direct treatment of inflammation and pain via prostaglandin pathways is how NSAIDs work, not the key action of combined contraceptives.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Receptor downregulation from steady, nonpulsatile GnRH exposure describes GnRH agonists such as leuprolide.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Inhibiting estrogen-synthesis enzymes is one of danazol's mechanisms, not the principal action of combined oral contraceptives.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old woman with severe endometriosis symptoms is started on sustained-release leuprolide. Her physician warns her that symptoms may briefly worsen before they improve. Which of the following best explains the eventual therapeutic effect of this drug?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Competitive blockade of the GnRH receptor prevents any rise in LH and FSH

choices.label: B
choices.text: Constant GnRH receptor stimulation downregulates the receptor, suppressing LH and FSH

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enhanced pulsatile GnRH secretion increases progesterone to oppose estrogen

choices.label: D
choices.text: Structural mimicry of sex steroids blocks implantation of ectopic tissue

choices.label: E
choices.text: Suppression of matrix metalloproteinases limits growth of ectopic endometrium

explanation.summary: GnRH agonists provide steady, nonpulsatile receptor stimulation that downregulates GnRH receptors and shuts off LH and FSH.
explanation.whyCorrect: GnRH agonists such as leuprolide replace pulsatile GnRH signaling with a steady level of agonist. After an initial transient flare of LH and FSH, GnRH receptors downregulate, leading to complete suppression of LH and FSH secretion, decreased estrogen, and a physiologic menopause-like state that shrinks endometriotic tissue.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Receptor antagonism without an acute gonadotropin increase describes GnRH antagonists; the flare this patient was warned about identifies an agonist.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Agonists abolish, rather than enhance, pulsatile GnRH signaling; the benefit comes from suppressing the axis, not raising progesterone.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A cholesterol-like structure acting at sex-hormone targets and blocking implantation describes danazol.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Suppression of matrix metalloproteinases is the mechanism of progestin-only agents.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman with endometriosis and a history of deep venous thrombosis is prescribed a hormonal agent considered safe given her clotting history. Which of the following is the mechanism by which this agent treats her endometriosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Creation of a steady nonpulsatile GnRH level

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct anti-inflammatory action on implant tissue

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inhibition of estrogen synthesis by a synthetic androgen

choices.label: E
choices.text: Suppression of ovulation by combined estrogen and progestin

explanation.summary: Progesterone-only agents, the preferred choice when estrogen is contraindicated, suppress matrix metalloproteinases.
explanation.whyCorrect: Patients who cannot take exogenous estrogen, such as those with a history of blood clots, are treated with progesterone-only agents. Progestins suppress matrix metalloproteinases, a class of enzymes important in the growth and implantation of endometrium, thereby limiting ectopic endometrial tissue.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A steady nonpulsatile GnRH level is how GnRH agonists work; that is not the estrogen-free agent chosen specifically for clot history in this context.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Direct treatment of inflammation is the mechanism of NSAIDs, which are not the hormonal agent described.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The synthetic androgen danazol inhibits estrogen-synthesis enzymes but carries androgenic effects and is not defined by safety in clotting disorders.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Combined estrogen-progestin contraceptives contain exogenous estrogen, which this patient must avoid because of her thrombosis history.

questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman treated for refractory endometriosis returns to clinic reporting new coarse facial hair, worsening acne, and deepening of her voice. Which of the following medications is the most likely cause of these findings?

explanation.summary: Danazol is a synthetic androgen, so its adverse effects include hirsutism, masculinization, and acne.
explanation.whyCorrect: Danazol has a chemical structure similar to cholesterol-based sex steroids, letting it act at many sex-hormone targets: it inhibits estrogen-synthesis enzymes, the LH surge, and implantation of ectopic tissue. Because it can be considered a synthetic androgen, androgen-related adverse effects such as hirsutism, masculinization, and acne are characteristic.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Combined estrogen-progesterone contraceptives suppress the LH surge and are not described as causing androgenic virilization.
whyWrongByChoice.C: GnRH antagonists suppress the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis by receptor blockade; androgen excess is not their characteristic effect.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ibuprofen is an NSAID used for pain and inflammation and does not cause hirsutism or masculinization.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Leuprolide creates a menopause-like state through receptor downregulation rather than androgenic side effects.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old postmenopausal woman presents with vaginal bleeding. Endometrial biopsy shows markedly crowded glands with complex architecture, open chromatin, and conspicuous nucleoli. She has no desire for future fertility. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Local excision of the lesion by curettage

explanation.summary: Atypical endometrial hyperplasia warrants hysterectomy because of a 30-50% chance of concurrent endometrial carcinoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: Crowded glands with complex architecture and cytologic atypia (open chromatin, conspicuous nucleoli) define atypical endometrial hyperplasia/EIN. These features overlap with well-differentiated endometrioid adenocarcinoma, and because 30-50% of patients harbor concurrent carcinoma, surgical hysterectomy is recommended when atypia is found and fertility is not desired.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Curettage for local excision is the treatment for endometrial polyps, not for hyperplasia with atypia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Progestins are first-line for hyperplasia without atypia; once atypia is present, the high risk of concurrent carcinoma makes hysterectomy the recommended treatment for a patient not seeking fertility.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Observation ignores a lesion with substantial risk of harboring carcinoma and is inappropriate.
whyWrongByChoice.E: GnRH agonists are used for severe endometriosis, not for atypical endometrial hyperplasia.

questions.stem: A 48-year-old perimenopausal woman with chronic anovulatory cycles presents with several months of heavy, irregular uterine bleeding. Endometrial biopsy shows an increased gland-to-stroma ratio with crowded glands but minimal cytologic atypia. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment?

explanation.summary: Nonatypical endometrial hyperplasia is treated first with progestins, which cause regression in most cases.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chronic anovulation during the perimenopausal transition removes progesterone's restraint on the estrogen-driven endometrium, producing hyperplasia. Biopsy showing crowded glands without atypia is nonatypical hyperplasia, which rarely progresses to adenocarcinoma (1-3%) and regresses with progestin therapy in most cases.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antibiotics treat endometritis; there is no evidence of infection here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hysterectomy is reserved for hyperplasia with atypia, where concurrent carcinoma risk is 30-50%; this biopsy shows no atypia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: NSAIDs address inflammatory menstrual pain and mild endometriosis, not proliferative overgrowth of the endometrium.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Unopposed estrogen is a cause of endometrial hyperplasia and would worsen the condition.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old woman taking tamoxifen after treatment for breast cancer reports intermittent irregular pelvic bleeding. Hysteroscopy shows a discrete, benign-appearing projection of glandular and stromal tissue extending into the endometrial cavity. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hysterectomy with removal of ovaries and tubes

explanation.summary: Endometrial polyps, which are associated with tamoxifen, are removed by local excision using curettage.
explanation.whyCorrect: A localized benign hyperplastic overgrowth of glands and stroma projecting into the endometrial cavity is an endometrial polyp. Polyps may arise in association with tamoxifen and can cause irregular pelvic bleeding; they are usually removed by local excision using curettage.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Clindamycin plus gentamicin is an empiric regimen for endometritis, an infectious process not present here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Removal of the uterus, ovaries, and tubes is treatment for severe refractory endometriosis or hyperplasia with atypia, far beyond what a benign polyp requires.
whyWrongByChoice.D: GnRH agonists treat severe endometriosis; they are not the treatment for a discrete polyp.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Progestins are first-line for endometrial hyperplasia, whereas a localized polyp is managed by excision.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman develops fever, malaise, uterine tenderness, and foul vaginal discharge 5 days after cesarean delivery complicated by retained placental fragments. Blood cultures are pending. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Await culture results before starting therapy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Obtain endometrial biopsy to look for plasma cells

explanation.summary: Acute pregnancy-related endometritis is treated promptly with empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics, most commonly clindamycin plus gentamicin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Postpartum endometritis is more frequent after cesarean delivery, and retained products of conception are the usual predisposing factor. Patients present acutely with discharge, bleeding, and constitutional symptoms. Empiric antibiotic therapy should begin promptly regardless of whether culture data are available; clindamycin plus gentamicin is the most common regimen, with piperacillin-tazobactam or ceftriaxone plus metronidazole as alternatives.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Empiric therapy should be initiated promptly regardless of culture availability; waiting delays needed treatment.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hormonal therapy treats endometriosis, not an acute uterine infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Plasma cells on biopsy diagnose chronic endometritis; acute endometritis is diagnosed clinically, and biopsy is not the next step in this acutely ill patient.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hysterectomy is not the management of acute postpartum endometritis, which responds to antibiotics.

questions.stem: During the second half of a normal menstrual cycle, the endometrium stops thickening further while its glands become tortuous and secretory. Which of the following best describes the action of progesterone on the endometrium at this time?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Promotes secretory differentiation and limits growth

choices.label: B
choices.text: Causes crowding of glands with cytologic atypia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Drives continued proliferative growth of the lining

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increases conversion of androgens to estrogen

choices.label: E
choices.text: Stimulates the midcycle surge of luteinizing hormone

explanation.summary: Estrogen makes the endometrium proliferate; progesterone drives secretory differentiation and restrains further proliferative growth.
explanation.whyCorrect: The endometrial lining proliferates in response to estrogen, while progesterone promotes secretory differentiation and limits further proliferative growth. The cyclic interplay of these two hormones produces the monthly build-up and shedding of endometrium, and an imbalance favoring estrogen over progesterone is what allows excessive endometrial growth.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Glandular crowding with cytologic atypia is the pathologic picture of atypical endometrial hyperplasia, not a normal progesterone effect.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Proliferative growth of the lining is the action of estrogen; progesterone opposes it.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Conversion of androgens to estrogen occurs in adipose tissue and contributes to hyperplasia; it is not an endometrial action of progesterone.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The midcycle LH surge is a pituitary event; progesterone does not trigger it, and combined contraceptives are used to suppress it.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman with 6 years of cyclic pelvic pain and infertility undergoes diagnostic laparoscopy for suspected endometriosis. Which of the following is the most common location for the implants of this condition?

explanation.summary: The most common sites of endometriotic implants are the ovary, pelvic peritoneum, uterosacral ligaments, and pouch of Douglas.
explanation.whyCorrect: Endometriosis is growth of endometrial cells implanted outside of the uterus, and the ovary heads the list of common implant sites along with the pelvic peritoneum, uterosacral ligaments, and pouch of Douglas. Repeated cyclic bleeding of ovarian implants is also what produces endometriomas (chocolate cysts).

whyWrongByChoice.A: The endocervix is relevant as a barrier to ascending infection in endometritis; it is not a characteristic site of endometriotic implants.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Pulmonary endometriosis does occur but is explicitly rare, explained by spread through vascular and lymphatic channels.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Endometrial tissue within the myometrium defines adenomyosis, a related but distinct disorder.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Implants can occur almost anywhere, but the vaginal mucosa is not among the common sites listed for endometriosis.

questions.stem: A 37-year-old woman with laparoscopically confirmed endometriosis reports 4 months of dysuria and urinary frequency that predictably worsen during her menses. Urinalysis and urine culture are negative. Which of the following best explains her urinary symptoms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adhesions encasing the ovaries and fallopian tubes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ascending bacterial infection of the endometrium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Estrogen-driven overgrowth of the endometrial lining

choices.label: E
choices.text: Endometriotic implants involving the bladder wall

explanation.summary: Endometriosis that extends to the bladder causes dysuria and urinary frequency, which flare cyclically with menses.
explanation.whyCorrect: Implants respond to cyclic hormones exactly as eutopic endometrium does, so symptoms track the menstrual cycle. When endometriosis extends to the bladder, the result is dysuria and urinary frequency; sterile urine argues against infection as the cause.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Fibrosis and adhesions around the ovaries and tubes explain the infertility of endometriosis, not dysuria and urinary frequency.
whyWrongByChoice.B: An ascending infection would be endometritis and would typically produce fever, discharge, and positive cultures rather than sterile cyclic dysuria.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Estrogen-driven endometrial overgrowth is endometrial hyperplasia, which presents with abnormal or excessive uterine bleeding.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Uterine contractions during menstruation cause the cramping pain of primary dysmenorrhea, not urinary symptoms.

questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman with endometriosis has been unable to conceive for 3 years. At laparoscopy, dense bands of connective tissue surround both ovaries and distort the fallopian tubes. Which of the following processes is most directly responsible for these findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Repeated inflammation, healing, and organizing hemorrhage

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chronic unopposed estrogen stimulation of the endometrium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Neutrophilic infiltration of the endometrial glands

choices.label: D
choices.text: Plasma cell infiltration of the endometrial stroma

explanation.summary: Infertility in endometriosis results from fibrosis and pelvic adhesions generated by cycles of inflammation, healing, and organizing hemorrhage.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ectopic implants bleed with each cycle. The alternating inflammation and healing, together with organizing hemorrhage, leads to fibrosis and pelvic adhesions (abnormal connective tissue) around the ovaries and fallopian tubes, which is how endometriosis causes infertility.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Unopposed estrogen produces endometrial hyperplasia with abnormal bleeding, not pelvic adhesions.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neutrophils in the stroma and glands are the hallmark of acute endometritis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Plasma cells in the endometrial stroma define chronic endometritis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Suppressing pulsatile GnRH signaling is a therapeutic effect of GnRH agonists, not a cause of adhesions.

questions.stem: An 18-year-old woman reports cramping lower abdominal pain on the first day of each menses, occasionally with mild nausea. The pain reliably resolves with over-the-counter ibuprofen. She has no pain with intercourse, and pelvic examination is normal. Which of the following best explains her pain?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Backward flow of menstrual blood into the peritoneal cavity

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ectopic endometrial implants on the pelvic peritoneum

choices.label: C
choices.text: Endometrial glands and stroma within the uterine wall

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neutrophils filling the endometrial glandular lumens

explanation.summary: Primary dysmenorrhea is pain from uterine contractions during menstruation, cramp-like, mild in associated symptoms, and responsive to over-the-counter NSAIDs.
explanation.whyCorrect: Dysmenorrhea and endometriosis both cause pelvic pain but differ in cause. Dysmenorrhea is primarily caused by uterine contractions during menstruation and is often a normal part of the menstrual cycle; the pain is cramp-like, may come with mild nausea or fatigue, and improves with ibuprofen. Endometriosis, by contrast, causes more severe chronic pain that can occur at any point in the cycle and is associated with dyspareunia and infertility.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Retrograde menstruation is a proposed mechanism for establishing endometriosis, a chronic condition requiring medical intervention, not for ordinary cyclic cramps.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Peritoneal implants would be expected to cause more severe chronic pain with dyspareunia and fertility problems, and pain poorly controlled by ibuprofen.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Endometrial tissue within the myometrium is adenomyosis, which presents with abnormal uterine bleeding and a diffusely enlarged, soft uterus.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neutrophils filling glandular lumens indicate acute endometritis, which presents with fever, pelvic pain, and discharge.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman undergoing laparoscopy for infertility is found to have implants of endometrial glands and stroma on the uterosacral ligaments and in the pouch of Douglas. According to the most widely accepted and historically dominant theory, how did endometrial tissue reach these sites?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Invagination of the basal endometrium into the uterine wall

choices.label: B
choices.text: Spread of endometrial cells through lymphatic channels

choices.label: C
choices.text: Transformation of peritoneal mesothelial cells into endometrium

choices.label: D
choices.text: Transport of bacteria upward past the endocervical barrier

choices.label: E
choices.text: Backward flow of menstrual blood through the fallopian tubes

explanation.summary: Retrograde menstruation is the most widely accepted theory for pelvic endometriotic implants.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the retrograde menstruation theory, endometrial tissue shed during the cycle flows backward through the fallopian tubes and migrates to the ovaries and the pelvic or peritoneal cavities, where it implants. This is the most widely accepted and historically dominant of the three proposed theories and fits implants confined to pelvic structures such as the uterosacral ligaments and pouch of Douglas.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Invagination of the basal endometrial layer into the myometrium is a proposed mechanism of adenomyosis, which stays within the uterine wall.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Lymphatic and vascular spread is a competing theory invoked mainly to explain distant implants such as pulmonary endometriosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Coelomic metaplasia is a real competing theory but is not the most widely accepted or historically dominant one.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ascending bacterial infection causes endometritis; it does not deposit endometrial glands and stroma in the pelvis.

questions.stem: In a laboratory experiment, cultured peritoneal mesothelial cells exposed to hormonal and immunologic stimuli acquire the appearance and behavior of endometrial cells. These findings provide the strongest support for which of the following explanations of endometriosis?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Invagination of the basal endometrial layer

explanation.summary: The coelomic metaplasia theory holds that hormonal or immunologic factors transform mesothelial cells outside the uterus into endometrial cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: Coelomic metaplasia postulates that hormonal or immunological factors stimulate cells outside the uterus, specifically peritoneal or visceral mesothelial cells, to transform into endometrial cells. An experiment in which mesothelial cells convert to endometrial-type cells under hormonal and immunologic stimulation is exactly this proposed mechanism, and requires no transport of endometrium from the uterus.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hematogenous spread requires endometrial cells to enter the circulation from the uterus and implant elsewhere; no cell transport occurs in this experiment.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Invagination of the basal endometrial layer into the myometrium is a proposed mechanism of adenomyosis, not of peritoneal disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lymphatic dissemination likewise depends on transport of shed endometrial cells, not on local transformation of mesothelium.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Retrograde menstruation requires menstrual tissue to flow backward through the tubes and implant; the experiment involves no menstrual tissue.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman with mild endometriosis is started on a medication that controls her pain and also acts directly on the inflammation generated by her implants. Which of the following was most likely prescribed?

explanation.summary: NSAIDs are the treatment for mild endometriosis that directly targets inflammation as well as pain.
explanation.whyCorrect: Medications are usually tried before surgery in endometriosis. Mild cases are treated with NSAIDs such as ibuprofen for pain control and direct treatment of the inflammation, which matters because endometriotic tissue overproduces prostaglandins and cytokines compared with normal endometrium.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Combined oral contraceptives work hormonally, chiefly by inhibiting the midcycle LH surge and suppressing ovarian function.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Danazol acts at sex-hormone targets, inhibiting estrogen synthesis and the LH surge and blocking implantation of ectopic tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Leuprolide downregulates GnRH receptors to suppress LH and FSH and is reserved for severe symptoms.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Progestin-only agents suppress matrix metalloproteinases involved in endometrial growth and implantation.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman with severe endometriosis is to begin therapy that suppresses the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis. Her physician specifically wants to avoid the transient worsening of symptoms that accompanies an initial rise in LH and FSH. Which of the following agents is most appropriate?

explanation.summary: GnRH antagonists suppress the axis by blocking the GnRH receptor, so there is no acute rise in LH or FSH and no flare.
explanation.whyCorrect: GnRH antagonists resemble agonists in suppressing the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis, but they do so by antagonizing the GnRH receptor, so there is no acute increase in LH or FSH. Agonists instead stimulate the receptor first, producing a transient flare of LH and FSH before receptor downregulation brings hormonal suppression.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Combined oral contraceptives suppress the LH surge but are not the agent defined by axis blockade without an initial gonadotropin rise.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Danazol is a synthetic androgen acting at sex-hormone targets, with androgenic adverse effects such as hirsutism and acne.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ibuprofen is an NSAID for pain and inflammation in mild disease and has no effect on the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Leuprolide is the prototypical GnRH agonist and causes exactly the transient LH and FSH flare being avoided.

questions.stem: A 39-year-old woman has received sustained-release leuprolide for 4 months for severe endometriosis, with substantial improvement in her pelvic pain. Which of the following sets of hormone levels is most likely at this point?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Elevated LH, elevated FSH, elevated estrogen

choices.label: B
choices.text: Elevated LH, elevated FSH, low estrogen

choices.label: C
choices.text: Low LH, low FSH, elevated estrogen

choices.label: D
choices.text: Low LH, low FSH, low estrogen

choices.label: E
choices.text: Normal LH, normal FSH, elevated progesterone

explanation.summary: Sustained GnRH agonist therapy downregulates GnRH receptors, giving complete suppression of LH and FSH with low estrogen.
explanation.whyCorrect: By providing a steady, nonpulsatile level of GnRH stimulation, agonists such as leuprolide downregulate GnRH receptors, leading to complete suppression of LH and FSH secretion and downregulation of estrogen. The result is a physiologic state of menopause created centrally, which is why gonadotropins are low rather than high.

whyWrongByChoice.A: High gonadotropins with high estrogen describes neither the drug's effect nor a menopausal state.
whyWrongByChoice.B: High gonadotropins with low estrogen is the pattern of primary ovarian failure; here the suppression is at the level of the pituitary.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Low gonadotropins with high estrogen is the opposite of the intended effect, since the goal is to remove estrogen stimulation of implants.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Normal gonadotropins with high progesterone would not suppress the cyclic hormone fluctuations that drive implant growth.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman has severe endometriosis that has not responded to NSAIDs, combined oral contraceptives, or a GnRH agonist. She has decided to proceed with surgery but wants to retain her ability to become pregnant. Which of the following is the most appropriate operation?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Excision of the endometriotic lesions alone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hysterectomy with preservation of the ovaries

choices.label: E
choices.text: Hysterectomy with removal of ovaries and tubes

explanation.summary: Conservative surgery removes only the endometriotic lesions and is chosen when fertility is to be preserved.
explanation.whyCorrect: Surgery is an option when endometriosis is severe and resistant to standard treatment. It can be conservative, removing only the lesions, in an attempt to preserve fertility; more severe cases are treated with removal of the uterus, ovaries, and fallopian tubes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Curettage scrapes tissue from inside the uterus and is used for endometrial polyps and for sampling the cavity, not for ectopic implants.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Removing both ovaries eliminates the patient's oocytes and defeats the goal of preserving fertility.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Removing the uterus ends any possibility of carrying a pregnancy, even with the ovaries left in place.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Removal of uterus, ovaries, and tubes is the definitive option for severe disease when fertility is not a consideration.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman has 5 years of cyclic pelvic pain and dyspareunia, and pelvic imaging findings suggest endometriosis. Historically, which of the following has been required to establish a definitive diagnosis of this condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Endometrial biopsy showing plasma cells in the stroma

choices.label: C
choices.text: Measurement of serum LH and FSH during the cycle

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cervical swab DNA probe for sexually transmitted infections

choices.label: E
choices.text: Hysteroscopy with curettage of the uterine cavity

explanation.summary: Definitive diagnosis of endometriosis historically required laparoscopic visualization with histologic confirmation, though many patients are now diagnosed clinically and by imaging.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because implants lie outside the uterine cavity, seeing them directly has been the diagnostic standard: laparoscopy with histologic confirmation of endometrial glands and stroma in an ectopic site. Many patients today are diagnosed and treated on clinical grounds supported by imaging, but surgical confirmation is the historical definitive test.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Plasma cells in the endometrial stroma establish chronic endometritis, a different disease of the uterine lining itself.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gonadotropin levels are not diagnostic of endometriosis; hormone manipulation is used for treatment, not diagnosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A DNA probe from a cervical swab is used when evaluating endometritis related to sexually transmitted infection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hysteroscopy with curettage samples the uterine cavity and is used to exclude uterine cancer in hyperplasia, not to find ectopic implants.

questions.stem: A 44-year-old woman reports heavy menstrual bleeding and increasingly painful periods over 2 years. On examination the uterus is diffusely enlarged and soft, with no discrete masses and no adnexal tenderness. Which of the following best describes the underlying abnormality?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Diffuse glandular crowding with an increased gland-to-stroma ratio

choices.label: B
choices.text: Endometrial glands and stroma within the myometrium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Endometrial glands and stroma on the pelvic peritoneum

choices.label: D
choices.text: Localized overgrowth of endometrium projecting into the cavity

choices.label: E
choices.text: Plasma cells and lymphocytes within the endometrial stroma

explanation.summary: Adenomyosis is endometrial tissue within the uterine wall, presenting with abnormal uterine bleeding, dysmenorrhea, and a diffusely enlarged, soft uterus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Adenomyosis is defined as the presence of endometrial tissue within the myometrium, possibly from invagination of the basal layer of the endometrium or metaplasia of remnant progenitor cells. It presents with abnormal uterine bleeding and dysmenorrhea, and the uterus is characteristically diffusely enlarged and soft on examination.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Glandular crowding with an increased gland-to-stroma ratio is nonatypical endometrial hyperplasia, which causes abnormal bleeding without a diffusely enlarged, soft uterus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Implants on the pelvic peritoneum are endometriosis, which produces dysmenorrhea, dyspareunia, and infertility rather than a uniformly boggy uterus.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A localized projection of glands and stroma into the cavity is an endometrial polyp, typically asymptomatic or causing irregular bleeding.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Plasma cells with lymphocytes in the stroma indicate chronic endometritis, which does not diffusely enlarge the uterus.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman with polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) has had only 3 menstrual periods in the past year. Endometrial biopsy performed because of heavy bleeding shows crowded glands without cytologic atypia. Which of the following best explains the development of this lesion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cyclic bleeding from implants outside the uterine cavity

choices.label: B
choices.text: Excess progesterone acting on an estrogen-primed endometrium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inflammation of the endometrium from an ascending infection

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prolonged estrogen stimulation unopposed by progesterone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Suppression of luteinizing hormone by exogenous progestins

explanation.summary: Chronic anovulation, as in PMOS, leaves the endometrium under prolonged unopposed estrogen stimulation and produces endometrial hyperplasia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Endometrial hyperplasia arises when estrogen is increased relative to progesterone, either from excess estrogen or from absence of progesterone. Anovulation is one of the listed causes of prolonged estrogenic stimulation, and PMOS is among the conditions associated with endometrial hyperplasia. Without ovulation there is no corpus luteum progesterone to limit proliferative growth, so the glands crowd and the lining overgrows.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Implants outside the uterine cavity are endometriosis and do not produce glandular crowding of the uterine lining.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Progesterone limits proliferation and is used therapeutically to make hyperplasia regress; its excess would not cause this lesion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Inflammation from ascending infection is endometritis, whose biopsy shows neutrophils or plasma cells rather than crowded glands.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Progestin-induced suppression of LH is a treatment effect and would oppose, not cause, endometrial overgrowth.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old woman with a BMI of 42 who completed menopause 10 years ago presents with vaginal bleeding. She takes no hormonal medications, and pelvic ultrasound shows no adnexal mass. Endometrial biopsy shows hyperplasia without atypia. Which of the following is the most likely source of the estrogen driving her endometrial lesion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Continued follicular estrogen production by the ovaries

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conversion of precursors to estrogen within adipose tissue

choices.label: C
choices.text: Estrogen secreted by a functional granulosa cell tumor

choices.label: D
choices.text: Exogenous estrogen replacement given without a progestin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pulsatile release of estrogen by the anterior pituitary

explanation.summary: Adipose tissue contains enzymes that generate estrogen, so increased adiposity is an endogenous source of the unopposed estrogen that drives hyperplasia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Excess estrogen causing endometrial hyperplasia can come from anovulation, endogenous production, or exogenous hormones. Increased adipose tissue is listed among the associated conditions because fat contains the enzymes that convert precursors into estrogen, which is especially important after menopause when ovarian output has ceased. Any postmenopausal woman with uterine bleeding should be suspected of having endometrial hyperplasia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Follicular estrogen production ends with menopause and cannot account for continued estrogen stimulation 10 years later.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A functional granulosa cell tumor is an endogenous estrogen source, but imaging shows no adnexal mass in this patient.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Prolonged unopposed estrogen replacement is a recognized cause, but this patient takes no hormonal medications.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Estrogen is not a pituitary hormone; the pituitary releases the gonadotropins LH and FSH.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old woman with a normal BMI who takes no medications presents with vaginal bleeding 14 years after menopause. Pelvic ultrasound shows a 6-cm solid right ovarian mass, and endometrial biopsy shows hyperplasia without atypia. Which of the following best explains her endometrial findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aromatization of androgens in excess adipose tissue

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cortical stromal hyperplasia involving both ovaries

choices.label: C
choices.text: Estrogen production by a functional ovarian tumor

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prolonged use of unopposed exogenous estrogen

choices.label: E
choices.text: Retrograde menstruation with implantation on the ovary

explanation.summary: Functional granulosa cell tumors of the ovary secrete estrogen and are an endogenous cause of endometrial hyperplasia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among the conditions associated with endometrial hyperplasia are functional granulosa cell tumors of the ovary, which produce estrogen and therefore drive prolonged estrogenic stimulation of the endometrium. A discrete solid ovarian mass in a postmenopausal woman with hyperplasia and no other estrogen source points to this hormonally active tumor.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Estrogen generated in adipose tissue requires increased adiposity; this patient has a normal BMI.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cortical stromal hyperplasia is a diffuse ovarian change rather than a discrete 6-cm solid mass.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Unopposed exogenous estrogen is a well-recognized cause, but the patient takes no medications.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Retrograde menstruation relates to endometriosis and cannot occur years after menopause.

questions.stem: A 59-year-old woman who completed menopause 7 years ago reports 2 months of intermittent vaginal bleeding. She feels well, and pelvic examination is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to establish the diagnosis?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reassure her and observe for 6 months

choices.label: E
choices.text: Send a cervical swab DNA probe

explanation.summary: Endometrial hyperplasia should be suspected in any postmenopausal woman with uterine bleeding, and the diagnosis is made by endometrial biopsy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Patients with endometrial hyperplasia experience abnormal or excessive uterine bleeding, and it should be suspected for any postmenopausal female with uterine bleeding. Diagnosis is made by endometrial biopsy, which also classifies the lesion as nonatypical hyperplasia or atypical hyperplasia/EIN, a distinction that determines treatment.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Progestins are the treatment for hyperplasia without atypia, but treating before biopsy would miss atypia or a concurrent carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Laparoscopy is used to visualize endometriotic implants outside the uterus, not to evaluate postmenopausal bleeding.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Observation is inappropriate because postmenopausal bleeding may signal hyperplasia progressing toward endometrial cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A DNA probe for sexually transmitted infections is used in suspected endometritis, not in postmenopausal bleeding.

questions.stem: An endometrial biopsy from a 57-year-old woman with postmenopausal bleeding shows crowded glands with complex architecture, rounded vesicular nuclei, and prominent nucleoli. Molecular testing of this lesion is most likely to reveal a mutation in which of the following genes?

explanation.summary: PTEN tumor suppressor mutations are common in atypical hyperplasia/EIN and in endometrioid carcinoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: Crowded glands with complex architecture and cytologic atypia, including open chromatin and conspicuous nucleoli, define atypical endometrial hyperplasia/endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia. Mutations in the PTEN tumor suppressor gene are common in this lesion and in endometrioid carcinoma, with which it shares considerable morphologic overlap.

whyWrongByChoice.A: APC is not the tumor suppressor gene associated with atypical endometrial hyperplasia and endometrioid carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.B: BRCA1 is not the gene identified with atypical hyperplasia/EIN in this setting.
whyWrongByChoice.C: NF1 has no established role in the endometrial hyperplasia-carcinoma sequence described here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: RB1 is not the tumor suppressor commonly mutated in atypical hyperplasia/EIN.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman with irregular heavy uterine bleeding has an endometrial biopsy showing atypical endometrial hyperplasia/endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia. She has never been pregnant and strongly wishes to conceive in the future. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hysterectomy with removal of both ovaries

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hysteroscopy with curettage to exclude carcinoma

explanation.summary: When atypical hyperplasia is found in a patient who wants to conceive, uterine cancer must first be excluded with hysteroscopy and curettage.
explanation.whyCorrect: Atypia carries a 30-50% chance of concurrent endometrial carcinoma, which is why hysterectomy is recommended when fertility is not a consideration. For those who might want to conceive, uterine cancer should first be ruled out with hysteroscopy (endoscopic visualization of the uterus) and curettage (removal of uterine tissue by scraping), which samples the cavity far more thoroughly than the office biopsy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hysterectomy is the recommended treatment for atypia but eliminates any chance of pregnancy, so it is not the next step in a patient seeking fertility.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Waiting a year leaves a lesion with a 30-50% chance of harboring carcinoma unevaluated.
whyWrongByChoice.D: GnRH agonists are used for severe endometriosis, not for atypical endometrial hyperplasia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Unopposed estrogen is a cause of endometrial hyperplasia and would worsen the lesion.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman who has never been pregnant presents with fever, pelvic pain, and vaginal discharge, and acute endometritis is diagnosed. Which of the following most likely preceded her illness?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Prolonged use of unopposed exogenous estrogen therapy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Radiation therapy directed at the pelvic organs

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pelvic inflammatory disease from a gonococcal infection

choices.label: D
choices.text: Retained products of conception after a delivery

choices.label: E
choices.text: Long-term treatment with tamoxifen for breast cancer

explanation.summary: Acute endometritis in a non-obstetric patient is usually preceded by pelvic inflammatory disease from a sexually transmitted infection or by an invasive gynecologic procedure.
explanation.whyCorrect: The endometrium and myometrium are relatively resistant to infection because the endocervix forms a barrier to ascending organisms. In the non-obstetric population, acute endometritis is usually preceded by pelvic inflammatory disease, either secondary to a sexually transmitted infection with Neisseria gonorrhoeae or Chlamydia trachomatis, or following an invasive gynecologic procedure. Patients present with fever, pelvic pain, and vaginal discharge.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Unopposed estrogen causes endometrial hyperplasia with abnormal bleeding, not an acute febrile infection.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Pelvic radiation is listed among causes of chronic endometritis, which is indolent rather than acutely febrile.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Retained products of conception predispose to pregnancy-related endometritis, but this patient has never been pregnant.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tamoxifen is associated with endometrial polyps, not with acute infection of the endometrium.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old woman with an intrauterine contraceptive device in place for 3 years reports several months of pelvic pain and intermenstrual bleeding. She is afebrile, and her vital signs are normal. Which of the following findings on endometrial biopsy would best establish the diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Crowded glands with an increased gland-to-stroma ratio

choices.label: B
choices.text: Endometrial glands and stroma within the myometrial wall

choices.label: C
choices.text: Neutrophils filling the endometrial glandular lumens

choices.label: D
choices.text: Plasma cells scattered within the endometrial stroma

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rounded vesicular nuclei with prominent nucleoli

explanation.summary: Chronic endometritis is diagnosed by endometrial biopsy showing plasma cells within the endometrial stroma.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chronic endometritis can follow infection, intrauterine foreign bodies or growths such as an intrauterine contraceptive device, polyp, or leiomyoma, and radiation therapy; in about one-third of cases no etiology is found. Patients may be asymptomatic or have abnormal uterine bleeding and pelvic pain. The diagnosis usually requires an endometrial biopsy demonstrating plasma cells in the stroma, with or without lymphocytes and eosinophils.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Glandular crowding with an increased gland-to-stroma ratio is endometrial hyperplasia, which is a proliferative rather than inflammatory lesion.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Endometrial tissue inside the myometrium defines adenomyosis and would not be established by an endometrial biopsy in this way.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neutrophils in the stroma and glandular lumens characterize acute endometritis, which presents with fever and acute symptoms.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Rounded vesicular nuclei with prominent nucleoli are the cytologic atypia of atypical hyperplasia/EIN.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman develops fever, malaise, and purulent vaginal discharge 6 days after a spontaneous abortion complicated by retained products of conception. Which of the following organisms are the most likely causes of her infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Candida albicans and other commensal yeasts

choices.label: B
choices.text: Group A and group B streptococci and staphylococci

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trichomonas vaginalis and other protozoal organisms

explanation.summary: Pregnancy-related endometritis, which follows abortion or delivery with retained products of conception, is caused by group A and B streptococci, staphylococci, and other bacteria.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pregnancy-related endometritis is an acute process usually seen in the post-abortion or postpartum period and is more frequent after cesarean delivery, with retained products of conception the usual predisposing factor. Causative agents include group A and group B streptococci, staphylococci, and other bacteria, and patients present acutely with discharge, bleeding, and constitutional symptoms such as fever, fatigue, and malaise.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Yeasts are not among the agents implicated in pregnancy-related endometritis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tuberculosis is listed as a cause of chronic endometritis, an indolent process rather than an acute post-abortion infection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gonococcal and chlamydial infection cause the pelvic inflammatory disease that precedes acute endometritis in non-obstetric patients.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Protozoal organisms are not described as causes of pregnancy-related endometritis.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman at term is about to undergo a scheduled cesarean delivery. Which of the following, given routinely at the time of delivery, is most likely to reduce her risk of developing endometritis?

explanation.summary: Routine antibiotic prophylaxis, usually a cephalosporin, at all cesarean deliveries may prevent endometritis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pregnancy-related endometritis is more frequent after cesarean section, and routine use of antibiotics, usually a cephalosporin, at all cesarean deliveries may prevent it. This is prevention of a bacterial infection, distinct from the empiric broad-spectrum regimens used once infection is established.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Combined oral contraceptives suppress cyclic ovarian hormones to treat endometriosis and have no role in preventing infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: NSAIDs treat pain and inflammation, most notably in mild endometriosis, and do not prevent bacterial endometritis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Progestins treat endometrial hyperplasia and endometriosis; they do not reduce infection risk after surgery.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The organisms implicated in pregnancy-related endometritis are bacteria such as streptococci and staphylococci, not fungi.

questions.stem: A 46-year-old woman with abnormal uterine bleeding has an endometrial biopsy showing an increased gland-to-stroma ratio with crowded glands and minimal cytologic atypia. She asks how likely this lesion is to progress to adenocarcinoma. Which of the following is the best estimate?

explanation.summary: Nonatypical endometrial hyperplasia rarely progresses to adenocarcinoma, in roughly 1-3% of cases.
explanation.whyCorrect: Nonatypical endometrial hyperplasia is characterized by an increased gland-to-stroma ratio, that is, more crowded glands, without significant cytologic atypia, and these lesions rarely progress to adenocarcinoma (1-3% of cases). This is why progestins, which cause regression in most cases, are appropriate first-line therapy rather than hysterectomy.

whyWrongByChoice.B: This overstates the risk for hyperplasia without atypia and corresponds to no figure given for these lesions.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 30-50% is the chance of concurrent endometrial carcinoma when the biopsy shows atypia, not the progression risk of nonatypical hyperplasia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A risk this high would mandate hysterectomy, which is not the recommended management for hyperplasia without atypia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Near-universal progression would make this lesion effectively a carcinoma, which contradicts its benign behavior and response to progestins.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old woman comes to the office because of intermittent vaginal spotting for 2 months. Menopause occurred at age 57 years. She has never been pregnant, and her BMI is 32. Pelvic examination is normal. Transvaginal ultrasonography shows a thickened endometrial stripe. Which of the following is required to establish the definitive diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Postmenopausal bleeding is the cardinal sign of endometrial cancer, and diagnosis requires an endometrial biopsy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ultrasound (intravaginal or hydro ultrasonography) can detect endometrial cancer, and in postmenopausal patients the cancer risk rises with endometrial thickness, but the lecture is explicit that diagnosis requires an endometrial biopsy. This patient also carries classic risk factors: late menopause, nulliparity, and obesity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Waiting delays tissue diagnosis in a postmenopausal woman with bleeding and a thickened endometrium, the main warning sign of endometrial cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Pap testing samples the cervix; it does not establish a diagnosis of endometrial pathology.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Definitive surgery is the treatment once cancer is confirmed, not the step that establishes the diagnosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hormonal therapy without a tissue diagnosis could mask or delay recognition of a carcinoma.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman with a BMI of 36 is diagnosed with well-differentiated endometrioid endometrial carcinoma. Which of the following best explains how her obesity contributed to this tumor?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adipose tissue increases peripheral conversion to estrogen

choices.label: B
choices.text: Adipose tissue secretes progesterone that drives glandular growth

choices.label: C
choices.text: Obesity accelerates menopause and shortens estrogen exposure

choices.label: D
choices.text: Obesity causes endometrial atrophy that precedes carcinoma

choices.label: E
choices.text: Obesity directly induces somatic TP53 mutations

explanation.summary: Type I endometrial cancer is driven by chronic estrogen exposure, and obesity raises estrogen through peripheral conversion in adipose tissue.
explanation.whyCorrect: The main risk factor for type I (endometrioid) tumors is chronic estrogen exposure, which drives endometrial growth through hyperplasia and atypical hyperplasia/EIN to carcinoma. Obesity contributes because adipose tissue increases peripheral conversion of estrogen.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Progesterone opposes estrogen-driven proliferation; the risk comes from estrogen excess, exemplified by estrogen replacement without progesterone.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Late menopause, which lengthens estrogen exposure, is the risk factor; a shortened exposure would lower risk.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Endometrial atrophy is the background for type II serous carcinoma, not the estrogen-driven type I pathway.
whyWrongByChoice.E: TP53 mutation characterizes type II serous (copy-number high) tumors, not the estrogen-driven mechanism of obesity.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old woman taking tamoxifen for estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer develops abnormal uterine bleeding. Ultrasonography shows a thickened endometrium with a polyp. Which of the following properties of tamoxifen best explains these findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Competitive antagonism of the endometrial estrogen receptor

choices.label: B
choices.text: Weak estrogen agonist activity at the uterine estrogen receptor

choices.label: C
choices.text: Induction of somatic mutations in the TP53 gene

choices.label: D
choices.text: Blockade of progesterone receptors in the endometrium

choices.label: E
choices.text: Increased aromatization of androgens in adipose tissue

explanation.summary: Tamoxifen is a SERM that antagonizes estrogen receptors in breast but acts as a weak estrogen agonist in the uterus.
explanation.whyCorrect: As a selective estrogen receptor modulator, tamoxifen is a competitive antagonist at the breast tissue estrogen receptor, but in the uterus it is a weak estrogen agonist. This can lead to endometrial proliferation, hyperplasia, and polyps, raising the risk of endometrial cancer.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Competitive antagonism describes tamoxifen's action in breast tissue, which is why it treats breast cancer; the uterine effect is the opposite.
whyWrongByChoice.C: TP53 mutations characterize serous carcinoma; the lecture does not attribute them to tamoxifen, which acts through estrogen receptor agonism.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tamoxifen modulates estrogen receptors, not progesterone receptors.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Peripheral conversion in adipose tissue is the mechanism by which obesity raises estrogen, not a tamoxifen effect.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old woman undergoes hysterectomy for a well-differentiated endometrioid endometrial carcinoma. Molecular analysis of the tumor is performed. The mutations most commonly found in this tumor type act to increase signaling through which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Loss of p53-mediated cell cycle control

choices.label: B
choices.text: The exonuclease domain of DNA polymerase epsilon

choices.label: C
choices.text: Loss of DNA mismatch repair activity

choices.label: E
choices.text: Amplification of the estrogen receptor gene itself

explanation.summary: The most common mutations in type I endometrioid carcinoma increase PI3K/AKT signaling.
explanation.whyCorrect: In type I (endometrioid) tumors, the most common mutations increase signaling through the PI3K/AKT pathway, which augments expression of estrogen receptor-dependent target genes in endometrial cells, fitting the estrogen-driven pathogenesis of these cancers.

whyWrongByChoice.A: TP53 disruption is the hallmark of serous (type II, copy-number high) carcinoma, not the most common alteration in endometrioid tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.B: POLE exonuclease mutations define the ultra-mutated TCGA subtype, a minority of endometrioid cancers, not the most common mutation class.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mismatch repair deficiency defines the hypermutated/MSI subtype and Lynch-associated tumors, not the most common alteration overall.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The lecture describes augmented expression of estrogen receptor-dependent target genes via PI3K/AKT, not amplification of the receptor gene.

questions.stem: A 48-year-old thin woman is diagnosed with an endometrioid endometrial carcinoma. Tumor sequencing shows an ultra-high mutation burden. Which of the following molecular findings in her tumor would predict the best prognosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Mutation in the exonuclease domain of the POLE gene

choices.label: B
choices.text: Somatic TP53 mutation with extensive copy-number changes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Defective mismatch repair with microsatellite instability

choices.label: D
choices.text: Low mutation rate with few copy-number abnormalities

choices.label: E
choices.text: Strong diffuse nuclear accumulation of p53 protein

explanation.summary: POLE ultra-mutated carcinomas have an exceptionally good prognosis with conventional therapy.
explanation.whyCorrect: The TCGA ultra-mutated subtype harbors mutations in the exonuclease domain of DNA polymerase epsilon (POLE), is usually endometrioid, and can present in younger, often thinner women. Patients with these lesions have an exceptionally good prognosis with conventional therapy, the best of the four molecular subtypes.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Copy-number high tumors with somatic TP53 mutations are aggressive and have the worst survival outcomes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hypermutated MSI tumors, including Lynch syndrome-associated cancers, carry an intermediate survival, not the best.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Copy-number low tumors also have an intermediate survival.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Diffuse p53 accumulation on immunohistochemistry marks serous-type lesions in the worst-prognosis copy-number high group.

questions.stem: A 46-year-old woman with Lynch syndrome develops heavy, prolonged menstrual bleeding, and endometrial biopsy shows endometrioid carcinoma. Molecular testing of her tumor is most likely to show which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: POLE exonuclease domain mutation with ultra-high mutation burden

choices.label: B
choices.text: Somatic TP53 mutation with high copy-number abnormalities

choices.label: C
choices.text: Low mutation rate with low copy-number abnormalities

choices.label: E
choices.text: Defective mismatch repair function with microsatellite instability

explanation.summary: Lynch syndrome is a disorder of mismatch repair, and its endometrial cancers fall in the hypermutated, microsatellite-unstable TCGA subtype.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hypermutated carcinomas with defective mismatch repair (MMR) protein function and microsatellite instability are the tumors associated with Lynch syndrome. They are typically endometrioid and account for 29% of low-grade and 54% of high-grade endometrioid carcinomas, with intermediate survival.

whyWrongByChoice.A: POLE ultra-mutated tumors form a separate subtype found in younger, thinner women and are not the Lynch-associated group.
whyWrongByChoice.B: TP53-mutant, copy-number high biology characterizes serous carcinoma, not Lynch-associated endometrioid tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Copy-number low tumors are associated with higher BMI or exogenous estrogen rather than Lynch syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Homologous recombination deficiency is not one of the mechanisms described for endometrial cancer in this lecture; Lynch syndrome involves mismatch repair.

questions.stem: A 73-year-old woman has postmenopausal bleeding. Endometrial biopsy shows malignant cells forming papillae and tufts with marked cytologic atypia arising in a background of atrophic endometrium. Immunohistochemistry shows strong, diffuse nuclear p53 staining. Disruptive mutation of which of the following genes is most likely present in this tumor?

explanation.summary: Serous endometrial carcinoma arises in atrophic endometrium and is highly associated with disruptive TP53 mutations.
explanation.whyCorrect: Papillae and tufts in an older woman with endometrial atrophy describe serous (type II) carcinoma. Serous endometrial carcinoma is highly associated with disruptive TP53 mutations, corresponding to the copy-number high molecular category, and shows nuclear accumulation of p53 protein on immunohistochemistry.

whyWrongByChoice.A: POLE mutations define the ultra-mutated subtype, which is mostly endometrioid and carries an exceptionally good prognosis, unlike this lesion.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Mismatch repair defects define the hypermutated endometrioid subtype associated with Lynch syndrome, not serous carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: PI3K/AKT-activating mutations are the most common alterations of type I endometrioid tumors, which mimic normal endometrial glands.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Type II tumors are nonestrogen-driven; estrogen receptor gene mutation is not the described mechanism.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old woman with biopsy-proven endometrial carcinoma undergoes evaluation. The tumor involves the uterine corpus and extends into the cervix, but there is no disease outside the uterus. Which of the following is the correct stage?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Stage cannot be assigned without lymph node sampling

explanation.summary: Endometrial carcinoma that involves the cervix is stage II.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the staging system for endometrial carcinoma, stage I is confined to the uterus, stage II involves the cervix, stage III extends outside the uterus but not outside the true pelvis, and stage IV extends outside the true pelvis or involves the bladder or rectal mucosa. Cervical involvement therefore makes this stage II.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Stage I requires carcinoma confined to the uterus without cervical involvement.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Stage III requires extension outside the uterus, which is absent here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Stage IV requires spread outside the true pelvis or involvement of bladder or rectal mucosa.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The stage in this system is defined by anatomic extent; cervical involvement itself assigns stage II.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman has heavy, prolonged menses, urinary frequency, and constipation. Ultrasonography shows multiple firm masses in submucosal, intramural, and subserosal locations of the uterus. Histologic examination of one of these masses would most likely show which of the following?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Papillae and tufts with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio

choices.label: C
choices.text: Irregular cells with hyperchromatic nuclei and many mitoses

choices.label: D
choices.text: Regular, well-differentiated spindle-shaped smooth muscle cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Concentric lamellated calcifications throughout the stroma

explanation.summary: Uterine leiomyomas are benign smooth muscle tumors showing well-differentiated, regular spindle cells, often with hyalinization.
explanation.whyCorrect: Multiple firm uterine masses in a premenopausal woman with heavy menses, urinary symptoms, and constipation are classic leiomyomas (fibroids), the most common benign tumor of the urogenital tract. Histology shows well-differentiated, regular, spindle-shaped smooth muscle cells associated with hyalinization.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Invasive malignant glands describe endometrioid adenocarcinoma, an endometrial rather than myometrial lesion.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Papillary growth with tufts and marked atypia describes serous carcinoma of the endometrium.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cellular irregularity, hyperchromatic nuclei, and numerous mitotic figures describe leiomyosarcoma, which is rare and typically postmenopausal.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Psammoma bodies are seen in serous and clear cell carcinomas, not in fibroids.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman with ultrasound-confirmed uterine fibroids reports heavy menstrual bleeding that interferes with work. She wishes to avoid any surgical procedure. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Placement of a levonorgestrel intrauterine device

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hysterectomy with removal of the uterus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Early radical surgery for presumed leiomyosarcoma

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tamoxifen therapy to shrink the fibroids

explanation.summary: Levonorgestrel IUDs (and combination OCPs) reduce the bleeding symptoms of fibroids without surgery.
explanation.whyCorrect: Both levonorgestrel intrauterine devices and combination oral contraceptive pills can reduce the bleeding symptoms associated with fibroids, making the IUD the appropriate nonsurgical choice for a patient whose chief problem is heavy bleeding.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Hysterectomy is a last option for fibroids, not first-line therapy in a woman who wants to avoid surgery.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Uterine artery embolization is one of the surgical/procedural options, which this patient wishes to avoid.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fibroids in a premenopausal woman without rapid enlargement do not suggest leiomyosarcoma, which typically occurs in postmenopausal women.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tamoxifen is a breast cancer drug that acts as a weak estrogen agonist in the uterus; it is not a fibroid treatment.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old woman has a rapidly enlarging uterine mass. Hysterectomy is performed, and the pathologist must decide whether the mass is a leiomyoma or a leiomyosarcoma. Which of the following sets of features is used to make this distinction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Tumor diameter, number of tumors, and uterine location

choices.label: B
choices.text: Nuclear atypia, mitotic index, and tumor necrosis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Degree of hyalinization, tumor color, and firmness

choices.label: D
choices.text: Presence of psammoma bodies and papillary architecture

choices.label: E
choices.text: Estrogen receptor status and p53 immunostaining

explanation.summary: Leiomyosarcoma is distinguished from leiomyoma by nuclear atypia, mitotic index, and tumor necrosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture states that the distinction from leiomyoma is based on nuclear atypia, mitotic index, and tumor necrosis. Leiomyosarcomas show irregular cells with hyperchromatic nuclei and numerous mitotic figures, whereas leiomyomas show regular, well-differentiated spindle cells.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Leiomyomas are often multiple and can be large; size, number, and location do not establish malignancy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hyalinization and a firm white cut surface are features of benign leiomyomas and do not separate the two.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Psammoma bodies and papillary growth belong to serous carcinoma of the endometrium, not smooth muscle tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Receptor status and p53 staining are discussed for endometrial carcinomas, not for grading myometrial smooth muscle tumors.

questions.stem: A 46-year-old woman is found to have a uterine smooth muscle tumor that extends into pelvic veins and reaches the inferior vena cava and right atrium. Resected tissue shows well-differentiated, regular smooth muscle cells without atypia, necrosis, or increased mitotic activity. Which of the following best describes this lesion?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Intravenous leiomyomatosis, a benign leiomyoma variant

explanation.summary: Intravenous leiomyomatosis is a benign leiomyoma variant that grows into vessels and can reach the vena cava and right atrium.
explanation.whyCorrect: Intravenous leiomyomatosis is an extremely rare variant of uterine leiomyoma that extends into vessels and spreads hematogenously, most commonly to the vena cava and the right atrium. Despite this unusual behavior it is considered benign, consistent with the bland, well-differentiated histology here.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Leiomyosarcoma would show nuclear atypia, a high mitotic index, and necrosis, all absent in this specimen.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This is a smooth muscle (myometrial) lesion, not a glandular endometrial carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Disseminated peritoneal leiomyomatosis presents as multiple small peritoneal nodules, not intravascular extension.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Serous carcinoma is an endometrial epithelial malignancy with papillae, tufts, and marked atypia, unlike this bland smooth muscle proliferation.

questions.stem: During an abdominal hysterectomy, a surgeon incises the uterine wall from its outer surface inward toward the uterine cavity. Which of the following lists the layers in the order they are encountered?

explanation.summary: The uterine wall from superficial to deep is serosa (perimetrium), myometrium, and endometrium.
explanation.whyCorrect: The three layers of the uterus from superficial to deep are the serosa (perimetrium), the myometrium, and the endometrium. This ordering underlies the tumor classification in this lecture: endometrial carcinomas arise from the innermost glandular layer, while leiomyomas and leiomyosarcomas arise from the middle muscular layer.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This is the deep-to-superficial sequence, the reverse of what an outside-in incision encounters.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The serosa is the outermost covering, so it cannot be reached last.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The myometrium lies between the serosa and the endometrium, not deep to the endometrium.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The serosa is superficial to the myometrium, not sandwiched between the muscular and glandular layers.

questions.stem: Endometrial cancer is the most common gynecologic malignancy in the developed world, affecting approximately 26 of 100,000 people annually. Approximately what proportion of cases occurs in postmenopausal women?

explanation.summary: Seventy-five percent of endometrial cancers occur in postmenopausal women, which is why postmenopausal bleeding is the cardinal symptom.
explanation.whyCorrect: Endometrial cancer is the most common gynecologic malignancy in the developed world, occurs in postmenopausal women in 75% of cases, and affects 26 of 100,000 people annually (compared with 124 per 100,000 for breast cancer). Because most patients are postmenopausal, abnormal uterine bleeding in a woman no longer having periods is the main presenting symptom.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This underestimates the postmenopausal predominance; the disease is far more concentrated after menopause.
whyWrongByChoice.B: About 25% is the share occurring in premenopausal women, not postmenopausal women.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The distribution is not evenly split between pre- and postmenopausal patients.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The disease does occur before menopause in a meaningful minority, where it presents as intermenstrual or heavy, prolonged bleeding.

questions.stem: A 44-year-old woman who is still menstruating reports bleeding between her periods for 4 months. Transvaginal ultrasonography shows an endometrial thickness of 9 mm. Which of the following is the most accurate interpretation of this ultrasound finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Endometrial thickness does not correlate with cancer risk before menopause

choices.label: B
choices.text: Endometrial thickness of this degree excludes carcinoma before menopause

choices.label: C
choices.text: A thickened endometrium confirms carcinoma in a premenopausal patient

choices.label: D
choices.text: Endometrial thickness predicts cancer risk equally before and after menopause

choices.label: E
choices.text: Endometrial thickness measurement substitutes for biopsy before menopause

explanation.summary: Endometrial thickness stratifies cancer risk only in postmenopausal patients; in premenopausal patients it does not correlate with risk.
explanation.whyCorrect: In postmenopausal patients, the risk of cancer increases as the endometrial thickness increases on transvaginal ultrasound.
