In premenopausal patients, endometrial thickness does not correlate with risk of cancer, so the measurement cannot be used to rule disease in or out here. Intermenstrual bleeding still warrants investigation to exclude endometrial pathology, and diagnosis requires endometrial biopsy.

whyWrongByChoice.B: No thickness value excludes carcinoma before menopause, because thickness and risk are not correlated in this group.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A thickened stripe does not confirm carcinoma in anyone; tissue diagnosis by biopsy is required.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The correlation between thickness and cancer risk applies to postmenopausal patients only.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ultrasonography can detect abnormalities, but diagnosis of endometrial cancer requires an endometrial biopsy.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman with obesity who has taken estrogen replacement therapy without progesterone for several years undergoes endometrial biopsy for heavy, prolonged menses. The biopsy shows atypical hyperplasia/endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia (EIN). Which of the following best describes this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A benign reactive change that carries no increased cancer risk

choices.label: B
choices.text: A pre-malignant lesion that may progress to endometrioid carcinoma

choices.label: C
choices.text: The direct precursor lesion of uterine serous carcinoma

choices.label: D
choices.text: An early leiomyoma arising within the endometrial cavity

choices.label: E
choices.text: An invasive, well-differentiated adenocarcinoma of the endometrium

explanation.summary: Atypical hyperplasia/EIN is the pre-malignant step in the estrogen-driven pathway to type I endometrioid carcinoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chronic estrogen exposure increases endometrial growth, which can proceed to hyperplasia, then atypical hyperplasia/endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia (EIN), which is considered a pre-malignant condition, and then to carcinoma. This patient's unopposed estrogen therapy and obesity are classic drivers of that sequence.

whyWrongByChoice.A: EIN is explicitly a pre-malignant condition, not a benign reactive change.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The precursor of serous carcinoma is endometrial intraepithelial carcinoma, a different lesion arising in atrophic endometrium.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Leiomyomas are smooth muscle tumors of the myometrium, not glandular endometrial lesions.
whyWrongByChoice.E: EIN lacks the invasive malignant glands that define endometrioid adenocarcinoma; it precedes that step.

questions.stem: A 74-year-old woman has postmenopausal bleeding. Endometrial biopsy shows markedly atypical cells with a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio lining the surfaces of endometrial glands without stromal invasion; the surrounding endometrium is atrophic. Immunohistochemistry shows strong, diffuse nuclear p53 expression. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Clear cell carcinoma with psammoma bodies

choices.label: E
choices.text: Simple endometrial hyperplasia from unopposed estrogen

explanation.summary: Endometrial intraepithelial carcinoma is the p53-abnormal precursor of serous carcinoma and shows surface involvement without stromal invasion.
explanation.whyCorrect: Endometrial intraepithelial carcinoma is the precursor to serous carcinoma: malignant cells with morphologic features identical to serous carcinoma line the surfaces of endometrial glands without obvious stromal invasion, and immunohistochemistry shows strong, diffuse expression of p53. The atrophic background in an older postmenopausal woman fits the type II pathway.

whyWrongByChoice.A: EIN belongs to the estrogen-driven type I pathway and arises on a background of hyperplasia, not atrophy, and is not defined by diffuse p53 accumulation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Endometrioid adenocarcinoma shows excessive, invasive malignant glands that mimic proliferative endometrium, not noninvasive surface involvement with p53 accumulation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Clear cell carcinoma is an invasive type II tumor; psammoma bodies are seen in only about 10% of these and are not described here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Simple hyperplasia reflects estrogen excess and lacks the marked cytologic atypia and p53 abnormality seen here.

questions.stem: Serous endometrial carcinoma differs from endometrioid endometrial carcinoma in the population it affects. Compared with women who have endometrioid carcinoma, women with serous carcinoma are typically which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: About 10 years older, with an atrophic endometrium

choices.label: B
choices.text: About 10 years younger, with an atrophic endometrium

choices.label: C
choices.text: About 10 years older, with endometrial hyperplasia

choices.label: D
choices.text: About 10 years younger, with endometrial hyperplasia

choices.label: E
choices.text: The same age, with endometrial hyperplasia

explanation.summary: Serous carcinoma occurs in women about 10 years older than those with endometrioid carcinoma and arises in atrophic endometrium.
explanation.whyCorrect: Serous endometrial carcinoma generally occurs in women who are about 10 years older than those with endometrioid endometrial carcinoma and usually arises in the setting of endometrial atrophy. This contrasts with the estrogen-driven type I pathway, in which carcinoma develops out of hyperplasia and atypical hyperplasia/EIN.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The age relationship is reversed; serous carcinoma affects an older group.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hyperplasia is the background of estrogen-driven endometrioid tumors, not of serous carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Both elements are wrong: serous patients are older, and their background endometrium is atrophic.
whyWrongByChoice.E: There is a consistent age difference of roughly a decade between the two tumor types.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old woman undergoes endometrial biopsy for postmenopausal bleeding. Microscopic examination shows excessive, invasive malignant glands that are well differentiated and closely mimic proliferative endometrial glands. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Endometrioid carcinoma, the most common endometrial cancer, is typically well differentiated and mimics proliferative endometrial glands.
explanation.whyCorrect: Most type I tumors are endometrioid endometrial carcinoma, which accounts for 75%-80% of endometrial cancers. Most are well differentiated and mimic proliferative endometrial glands, the feature from which they take their name, and invasive examples show excessive, invasive malignant glands.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Serous carcinoma, a type II tumor, does not look like normal endometrial tissue; it forms papillae and tufts with marked atypia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Clear cell carcinoma is the other common type II tumor and likewise does not resemble normal endometrial glands.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Leiomyosarcoma is a malignant smooth muscle tumor of the myometrium composed of irregular spindle cells, not glands.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Endometrial intraepithelial carcinoma lines gland surfaces without stromal invasion and is the precursor of serous carcinoma.

questions.stem: A 75-year-old woman undergoes hysterectomy for endometrial carcinoma. Microscopic examination shows papillary architecture with numerous concentric, lamellated calcified structures. These structures are found in approximately 60% of which of the following tumors?

explanation.summary: Psammoma bodies are concentric lamellated calcifications seen in about 60% of uterine serous carcinomas.
explanation.whyCorrect: Psammoma bodies are concentric lamellated calcified structures seen in 60% of uterine serous carcinomas and only 10% of clear cell carcinomas. Their presence alongside papillary growth fits serous carcinoma, the most common type II endometrial cancer.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Clear cell carcinoma contains psammoma bodies in only about 10% of cases, far below the stated frequency.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Endometrioid carcinoma mimics proliferative endometrial glands and is not characterized by psammoma bodies.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Leiomyomas show regular spindle-shaped smooth muscle cells with hyalinization, not calcified lamellated bodies.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Leiomyosarcoma is defined by nuclear atypia, high mitotic index, and necrosis, not psammoma bodies.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman is evaluated after resection of a soft tissue sarcoma. Her mother had breast cancer at age 31 years, her brother had leukemia in childhood, and a maternal uncle had an adrenal tumor. An autosomal dominant cancer predisposition syndrome caused by inheritance of one aberrant copy of a gene on chromosome 17 is suspected. A germline mutation in which of the following genes is most likely present?

explanation.summary: Li-Fraumeni syndrome results from a germline TP53 mutation and produces early-onset breast cancer, sarcomas, leukemia, and brain and adrenal tumors.
explanation.whyCorrect: TP53, located on chromosome 17, encodes the p53 tumor suppressor, the guardian of the genome, which participates in DNA repair and cell cycle control. People who inherit one aberrant copy through a germline mutation usually develop tumors in early adulthood; this autosomal dominant condition is Li-Fraumeni syndrome, characterized by early-onset breast cancer, soft tissue sarcomas, leukemia, and brain and adrenal tumors.

whyWrongByChoice.B: POLE exonuclease domain mutations are somatic alterations defining the ultra-mutated endometrial carcinoma subtype, not an inherited multi-tumor syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Germline mismatch repair defects cause Lynch syndrome, whose tumor spectrum includes hypermutated endometrioid carcinoma rather than this constellation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: PI3K/AKT-activating mutations are the most common somatic changes in type I endometrial carcinoma and are not described as a germline syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Estrogen receptor signaling drives type I endometrial tumors, but no inherited receptor-gene syndrome is described.

questions.stem: A 76-year-old woman has serous endometrial carcinoma that invades the myometrium and involves the fallopian tubes and ovaries. Metastatic disease is most likely to be found in which of the following lymph node groups?

explanation.summary: Type II endometrial carcinomas invade the myometrium, spread to adjacent reproductive organs, and metastasize to pelvic or para-aortic lymph nodes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Type II tumors have an unfavorable prognosis and frequently invade the myometrium, spread to adjacent reproductive organs such as the fallopian tubes, ovaries, and vagina, and metastasize to pelvic or para-aortic lymph nodes. This nodal pattern is why cancer hysterectomy includes removal of surrounding lymph nodes from a broad abdominal and pelvic field.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Axillary nodes drain the breast and upper limb and are not the described route for endometrial carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Inguinal nodes are not the described nodal basin for endometrial carcinoma spread.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Supraclavicular involvement is not the pattern described for spread of these tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mediastinal nodes are not the regional basin involved by endometrial carcinoma.

questions.stem: A 54-year-old woman with a BMI of 37 who has taken exogenous estrogen is found to have a low-grade endometrioid endometrial carcinoma. Tumor sequencing shows a low mutation rate and a low frequency of DNA copy-number abnormalities. Approximately what percentage of low-grade endometrioid carcinomas fall into this molecular category?

explanation.summary: The copy-number low TCGA subtype makes up about 60% of low-grade endometrioid carcinomas and typically occurs in younger patients with higher BMI or exogenous estrogen.
explanation.whyCorrect: Carcinomas with low mutation rates and low-frequency DNA copy-number abnormalities comprise 60% of low-grade endometrioid carcinomas, 9% of high-grade endometrioid carcinomas, 2% of serous carcinomas, and 25% of mixed histology carcinomas. They have intermediate survival and often present in younger patients with higher BMI or exogenous estrogen, exactly this patient's profile.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Two percent is the share of serous carcinomas that fall into the copy-number low category.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Nine percent is the copy-number low share of high-grade, not low-grade, endometrioid carcinomas.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Twenty-five percent is the copy-number low share of mixed histology carcinomas.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Greater than 95% describes serous carcinomas falling into the copy-number high, TP53-mutated group.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old woman with biopsy-proven endometrial carcinoma undergoes staging evaluation. Cystoscopy shows tumor involving the mucosa of the bladder. There is no evidence of disease outside the true pelvis. Which of the following is the correct stage?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Stage III, because disease remains within the true pelvis

explanation.summary: Involvement of bladder or rectal mucosa defines stage IV endometrial carcinoma regardless of pelvic confinement.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the staging system for endometrial carcinoma, stage IV is carcinoma that extends outside the true pelvis OR involves the mucosa of the bladder or rectum. Mucosal bladder involvement therefore assigns stage IV even though the tumor has not left the true pelvis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Stage I requires carcinoma confined to the uterus.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Stage II requires cervical involvement without the mucosal invasion described here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Stage III describes extension outside the uterus but not outside the true pelvis, without bladder or rectal mucosal involvement.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pelvic confinement does not override the criterion of bladder or rectal mucosal involvement, which alone defines stage IV.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old woman has endometrioid endometrial carcinoma that appears confined to the uterus. Which of the following is the best treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hysterectomy with removal of the tubes, ovaries, and surrounding lymph nodes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pelvic radiation alone with surveillance imaging every 3 months

choices.label: C
choices.text: Combination chemotherapy alone with hormonal maintenance therapy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Progestin therapy alone with repeat endometrial biopsy in 6 months

choices.label: E
choices.text: Endometrial ablation with placement of a levonorgestrel intrauterine device

explanation.summary: The best treatment for endometrial cancer is surgical: removal of the uterus, fallopian tubes, ovaries, and surrounding lymph nodes.
explanation.whyCorrect: The best treatment is surgical, with removal of the uterus, fallopian tubes, ovaries, and surrounding lymph nodes; radiation or chemotherapy may be added. Most women are diagnosed with disease confined to the uterus, which carries 5-year survival exceeding 80%-90% after such treatment.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Radiation is an adjunct that may be added to surgery, not the primary treatment.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Chemotherapy is likewise an addition to surgical management rather than a substitute for it.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Anti-estrogen agents such as progestins produce variable responses and are not routinely used, let alone as sole therapy for cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ablation and a levonorgestrel IUD address bleeding from benign disease such as fibroids and do not treat carcinoma.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman with endometrioid endometrial carcinoma asks about treatment with anti-estrogen agents such as progestins. Which of the following best describes the role of these agents in this disease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They may produce a response because the tumor is estrogen driven, but the response is variable, so they are not used routinely

choices.label: B
choices.text: They are standard first-line therapy for all stages of disease, with surgery reserved for cases that recur afterward

choices.label: C
choices.text: They are ineffective in this tumor because endometrioid carcinoma does not depend on hormonal stimulation for growth

choices.label: D
choices.text: They are reserved for serous carcinoma, which responds to hormonal manipulation more reliably than endometrioid tumors do

choices.label: E
choices.text: They reliably eradicate disease confined to the uterus and therefore eliminate the need for surgical management

explanation.summary: Because endometrioid cancer is estrogen driven, it may respond to progestins, but variable response keeps them out of routine use.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because endometrioid cancer is caused in part by unopposed estrogen, it may sometimes respond to hormonal therapy such as anti-estrogen agents (progestins). The response is variable, so these agents are not routinely used; the best treatment remains surgical, with radiation or chemotherapy added as needed.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Surgery, not hormonal therapy, is the primary treatment for endometrial carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Endometrioid carcinoma is specifically the estrogen-driven type, which is why a hormonal response is possible at all.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Serous carcinoma is a nonestrogen-driven type II tumor and is not the target of anti-estrogen therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hormonal responses are variable and unreliable, and disease confined to the uterus is treated surgically.

questions.stem: A 67-year-old woman requires hysterectomy for endometrial carcinoma. Her surgeon plans an open abdominal or robotic approach rather than a vaginal hysterectomy. Which of the following best explains this choice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The uterus and cervix cannot be removed together through a vaginal approach

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lymph nodes must be removed from a broader region of the abdomen and pelvis

choices.label: C
choices.text: The ovaries must be left in place whenever a vaginal approach is used

choices.label: D
choices.text: Laparoscopic and robotic approaches are contraindicated in malignant disease

choices.label: E
choices.text: Endometrial biopsy cannot be performed before a vaginal hysterectomy

explanation.summary: Cancer surgery favors robotic or open approaches because lymph nodes must be taken from a broad abdominal and pelvic field.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hysterectomy can be performed abdominally (open), laparoscopically or robotically, or vaginally. For most cancer surgeries, robotic or open approaches are preferred because of the need to remove lymph nodes from a broader anatomical region of the abdomen and pelvis, which fits the pelvic and para-aortic spread pattern of endometrial carcinoma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A vaginal hysterectomy can remove the uterus, tubes, and ovaries through the vaginal opening; removal of the cervix is not the limiting factor.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The uterus, tubes, and ovaries can all be removed through a vaginal approach; whether the ovaries are removed defines full versus partial hysterectomy, not the route.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Robotic surgery is one of the preferred approaches for cancer, not a contraindicated one.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Endometrial biopsy is the diagnostic step performed before surgery regardless of the operative approach chosen.

questions.stem: A 43-year-old woman undergoes hysterectomy for symptomatic fibroids and asks that her ovaries be preserved. The operative note describes removal of the uterus, cervix, and fallopian tubes, with both ovaries left in place. This operation is best described as which of the following?

explanation.summary: A partial hysterectomy removes the uterus, cervix, and fallopian tubes but leaves the ovaries in place.
explanation.whyCorrect: A partial hysterectomy often means removal of the uterus, cervix, and fallopian tubes while leaving the ovaries in place, which is what this patient requested. A full hysterectomy usually implies removal of the uterus, cervix, fallopian tubes, and ovaries.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A full hysterectomy also removes the ovaries, which were deliberately preserved here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Excision of fibroids alone leaves the uterus in place, whereas the uterus was removed.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Embolization is a nonexcisional procedure that treats fibroids without removing any organ.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Removing only the tubes and ovaries would neither remove the uterus nor preserve the ovaries.

questions.stem: A 69-year-old woman with endometrial carcinoma is found on staging to have distant metastases. Which of the following 5-year survival rates is most appropriate to use in counseling her?

explanation.summary: Five-year survival for endometrial cancer falls from over 80%-90% for uterine-confined disease to about 15% with distant metastases.
explanation.whyCorrect: Most women with endometrial cancer are diagnosed with disease confined to the uterus, which carries excellent 5-year survival exceeding 80%-90%. When distant metastases are present, the 5-year survival rate drops sharply to about 15%. Overall, roughly 20%-25% of patients die of the disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Rates exceeding 80%-90% apply to disease confined to the uterus, not metastatic disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This also reflects the favorable, uterine-confined survival range.
whyWrongByChoice.C: About 40% is the overall 5-year survival for uterine leiomyosarcoma, a different tumor.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Survival with distant metastases is poor but substantially better than this figure.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old woman undergoes hysterectomy for a rapidly enlarging uterine mass, and pathology shows an anaplastic leiomyosarcoma. Compared with an overall 5-year survival rate of about 40% for leiomyosarcoma, the expected 5-year survival for anaplastic lesions is closest to which of the following?

explanation.summary: Leiomyosarcoma carries an overall 5-year survival of about 40%, but anaplastic lesions fall to 10%-15%.
explanation.whyCorrect: Leiomyosarcomas are rare, invasive cancers of the myometrium with a high fatality rate. The overall 5-year survival rate is about 40%, but the anaplastic lesions have a 5-year survival rate of only 10% to 15%, which is why early surgery is recommended before metastatic disease develops.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Survival exceeding 80% describes endometrial carcinoma confined to the uterus, not anaplastic leiomyosarcoma.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This exceeds even the overall leiomyosarcoma survival rate of about 40%.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This approximates the overall figure rather than the markedly worse anaplastic subgroup.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Survival is poor but not this low; a minority of patients with anaplastic lesions survive 5 years.

questions.stem: Leiomyomas are the most common benign tumor of the urogenital tract and are seen mostly in premenopausal women. Approximately what proportion of women are affected during their lifetime?

explanation.summary: Uterine leiomyomas affect 60%-70% of women during their lifetime and are usually asymptomatic.
explanation.whyCorrect: Leiomyomas are the most common benign tumor of the urogenital tract, affecting 60%-70% of women during their lifetime, and they are seen mostly in premenopausal women. Fibroids are usually asymptomatic; symptoms depend on the number, size, and location of the lesions.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This greatly understates the lifetime frequency of a tumor found in the majority of women.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fibroids are considerably more common than this over a lifetime.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This is still below the stated lifetime prevalence.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Prevalence is high but does not approach near-universal occurrence.

questions.stem: A 39-year-old woman has heavy, prolonged menses. Ultrasonography shows a firm, white uterine mass that bulges into the endometrial cavity. Which of the following terms best describes the location of this leiomyoma?

explanation.summary: Submucosal leiomyomas are those that bulge into the endometrial cavity.
explanation.whyCorrect: Leiomyomas occur in submucosal (bulging into the endometrial cavity), intramural, and subserosal locations and display a firm white appearance on sectioning. A mass bulging into the cavity is submucosal, and the bleeding pattern typical of fibroids is heavy and/or prolonged menses.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Subserosal fibroids sit beneath the outer serosal surface, projecting away from the cavity.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Intramural fibroids lie within the myometrial wall without bulging into the cavity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Perimetrium is another name for the serosa, the outermost layer, not a cavity-bulging location.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Peritoneal nodules describe disseminated peritoneal leiomyomatosis, a rare variant outside the uterus.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman has mild pelvic discomfort. Ultrasonography shows several small uterine fibroids. Her menses are normal in volume and duration, and her hemoglobin concentration is normal. Which of the following is the best initial treatment?

explanation.summary: Mild fibroid disease is treated first with pain relief using NSAIDs.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mild fibroid disease can be treated with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs for pain relief, which is the best initial treatment for uterine fibroids. Escalation to hormonal therapy or procedures is reserved for patients whose symptoms, particularly bleeding or mass effects, are not controlled.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Hysterectomy is a last option for fibroids, not an initial treatment for mild discomfort.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Embolization is a procedural option for symptoms that persist beyond conservative measures.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Surgical excision is likewise reserved for symptoms not controlled with simpler measures.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Oral contraceptives reduce fibroid-associated bleeding, but this patient's menses are normal and her problem is pain.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old woman has pelvic pressure and urinary frequency. Bimanual examination shows an irregularly enlarged uterus. Which of the following is the most appropriate test to diagnose uterine fibroids?

explanation.summary: Fibroids are best diagnosed with ultrasonography.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fibroids are best diagnosed with ultrasonography, which demonstrates the number, size, and location of the lesions responsible for symptoms such as pelvic pressure and urinary urgency or frequency from mass effect. Tissue sampling is not required to make the diagnosis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Endometrial biopsy is the test that establishes a diagnosis of endometrial cancer, prompted by intermenstrual or postmenopausal bleeding.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pap testing screens the cervix and says nothing about myometrial masses.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hysterectomy is a last-option treatment for fibroids, not a diagnostic test.
whyWrongByChoice.E: No hormone level is used to diagnose fibroids.

questions.stem: A 41-year-old woman with a history of uterine leiomyomas undergoes laparoscopy for pelvic pain. Numerous small nodules are found studding the peritoneal surfaces. Biopsy of several nodules shows well-differentiated smooth muscle cells without nuclear atypia, mitotic activity, or necrosis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stage III endometrioid carcinoma with peritoneal spread

explanation.summary: Disseminated peritoneal leiomyomatosis presents as multiple small peritoneal nodules and is benign despite its unusual distribution.
explanation.whyCorrect: Disseminated peritoneal leiomyomatosis is a rare leiomyoma variant that presents as multiple small peritoneal nodules and, like intravenous leiomyomatosis, is considered benign despite its unusual behavior. The bland, well-differentiated smooth muscle without atypia, mitoses, or necrosis confirms a benign smooth muscle proliferation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Leiomyosarcoma is distinguished by nuclear atypia, a high mitotic index, and tumor necrosis, all absent here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Intravenous leiomyomatosis extends into vessels and spreads hematogenously to sites such as the vena cava and right atrium, not across peritoneal surfaces.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Endometrioid carcinoma is a glandular epithelial malignancy, not a bland smooth muscle proliferation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Serous carcinoma shows papillae, tufts, and marked cytologic atypia, and psammoma bodies are not described here.

questions.stem: A 64-year-old woman who underwent menopause at age 52 years reports increasing pelvic fullness. Ultrasonography shows a myometrial mass that has enlarged rapidly over the past 4 months. Imaging shows no evidence of distant disease. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs with reassessment in 6 months

choices.label: C
choices.text: Placement of a levonorgestrel intrauterine device

choices.label: E
choices.text: Observation with repeat ultrasonography in 1 year

explanation.summary: A rapidly enlarging myometrial mass in a postmenopausal woman suggests leiomyosarcoma, for which early surgery is recommended.
explanation.whyCorrect: Leiomyosarcomas may present similarly to leiomyomas but typically occur in postmenopausal women and often demonstrate rapid enlargement. Early surgery is recommended because metastatic leiomyosarcoma may not be amenable to resection, and the overall 5-year survival is only about 40%.

whyWrongByChoice.B: NSAIDs treat pain from mild fibroid disease; they would delay resection of a possible sarcoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A levonorgestrel IUD reduces fibroid-related bleeding and does not address a suspected malignant myometrial tumor.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Embolization is a treatment option for symptomatic fibroids, not for a lesion suspicious for leiomyosarcoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Waiting a year risks progression to metastatic disease that may no longer be resectable.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman reports two months of unusually heavy menstrual bleeding and a cycle that has lengthened from 28 to 40 days. Pelvic ultrasound shows a 4-cm thin-walled, fluid-filled right ovarian cyst. The cyst later resolves without treatment. Which cell type in the wall of this lesion was most likely responsible for her menstrual symptoms?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ectopic endometrial cells shedding old blood

explanation.summary: Follicular cysts are lined by granulosa cells whose estrogen causes menorrhagia or lengthened cycles.
explanation.whyCorrect: A thin-walled, fluid-filled cyst in a menstruating woman that resolves spontaneously is a follicular cyst. Its wall is made of theca and granulosa cells, and the granulosa cells make estrogen, which can produce menstrual irregularities such as heavy bleeding or a longer cycle.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Theca lutein cells are stimulated by hCG from placental disorders like hydatidiform mole, not part of a simple follicular cyst.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Luteinized theca cells producing progesterone characterize a corpus luteum cyst, which delays menses rather than causing heavy bleeding from estrogen.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ectopic endometrial tissue defines an endometrioma, which causes pelvic pain with menstruation and contains old blood, not a simple resolving cyst.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A spontaneously resolving thin-walled cyst in a premenopausal woman is functional, not neoplastic.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman whose menstrual period is 10 days late develops sudden severe lower abdominal pain with nausea. A urine pregnancy test is negative. Ultrasound shows free fluid in the pelvis and a collapsed cystic structure on the left ovary with a yellow, convoluted wall noted at surgery. Which of the following best explains her delayed menses?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Continued progesterone production by theca cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Excess estrogen production by granulosa cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: hCG stimulation of the theca lutein layer

choices.label: D
choices.text: Elevated LH stimulation of theca interna cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Aromatization of androstenedione in adipose tissue

explanation.summary: Corpus luteum cysts persist beyond the normal 14 days, and their theca cells keep making progesterone, delaying menstruation; rupture can cause severe intraperitoneal bleeding.
explanation.whyCorrect: The yellow convoluted cyst wall and rupture with intraperitoneal blood loss describe a corpus luteum cyst, which arises when the corpus luteum abnormally persists after ovulation. Its luteinized theca cells may continue producing progesterone, which delays the onset of normal menstruation.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Granulosa-cell estrogen from a follicular cyst causes menorrhagia or a longer cycle, but the yellow luteinized wall and hemorrhagic rupture point to the corpus luteum.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Theca lutein cysts require high hCG from placental disorders such as molar pregnancy; her pregnancy test is negative.
whyWrongByChoice.D: LH-driven theca interna androgen production is the mechanism of PMOS, a bilateral disorder of small unruptured follicles, not a single ruptured cyst.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Peripheral aromatization to estrone is part of PMOS pathophysiology and does not explain a hemorrhagic luteal cyst.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman with a recently evacuated hydatidiform mole is found on ultrasound to have bilaterally enlarged ovaries containing multiple large cysts. Her serum testosterone precursor levels are elevated. Which of the following is the most likely course of these ovarian lesions?

explanation.summary: Theca lutein cysts are driven by hCG from placental disorders and recede when hCG levels decrease.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hydatidiform mole and choriocarcinoma secrete large amounts of hCG, which stimulates the theca lutein layer of the corpus luteum to form theca lutein cysts. These cells make androstenedione, explaining the high androgen levels, and the cysts enlarge and then recede as hCG falls.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Endometrial carcinoma risk relates to unopposed estrogen in PMOS, not to hCG-driven theca lutein cysts.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Torsion is a possible complication of ovarian masses but is managed urgently when it occurs, and these cysts are expected to recede rather than warrant prophylactic surgery.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Bilateral oophorectomy is reserved for patients with cancer, whereas theca lutein cysts resolve as the hCG source is treated.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Chocolate cysts are endometriomas filled with old blood from endometriosis, a different disease process.

questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman has several years of pelvic pain that is worst during menstruation. Laparoscopy reveals an ovarian cyst filled with thick brown-black material. Which of the following processes best accounts for the color of the cyst contents?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Breakdown of old blood into hemosiderin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Accumulation of clear straw-colored follicular fluid

choices.label: D
choices.text: Necrosis from twisting of the vascular pedicle

choices.label: E
choices.text: Secretion of mucin by neoplastic epithelium

explanation.summary: Endometriomas are chocolate cysts: ectopic endometrial tissue on the ovary bleeds, and the old blood breaks down to hemosiderin, producing a brown to black color.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pelvic pain that peaks with menstruation plus a cyst of old brown-black blood describes an endometrioma, which forms when endometriosis deposits on the ovary. The old blood is broken down to hemosiderin, giving the classic chocolate cyst appearance.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Luteinized granulosa cells give the corpus luteum cyst a pink hue, not brown-black contents.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Clear to straw-colored fluid fills a follicular cyst, which is thin-walled and not associated with menstrual pain of this type.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Torsion causes sudden severe unilateral pain from ischemia, not chronic cyclic pain with old blood in a cyst.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Neoplastic cysts arise with ovarian tumors and are suspected in postmenopausal patients; the lecture ties brown-black contents to endometriosis.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman with a known 6-cm right ovarian dermoid cyst presents with sudden-onset severe right lower quadrant pain, nausea, and vomiting. The pain has waxed and waned over several hours. Transvaginal ultrasound with Doppler shows preserved arterial flow to the right ovary. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Urgent laparoscopy with detorsion of the ovary

choices.label: B
choices.text: Observation with a repeat ultrasound in 3 months

choices.label: C
choices.text: Serum CA 125 measurement to rule out malignancy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Combined oral contraceptives for cyst suppression

explanation.summary: Ovarian torsion is a gynecologic emergency; normal Doppler flow does not exclude it, and management is urgent surgery, usually laparoscopic detorsion with ovarian preservation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sudden severe unilateral pain with nausea and vomiting in a woman with an ovarian mass over 5 cm, with intermittent pain suggesting partial torsion, is torsion until proven otherwise. Diagnosis is primarily clinical, normal flow on Doppler does not exclude torsion, and urgent laparoscopic detorsion prevents necrosis and preserves fertility.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Serial observation suits asymptomatic incidental cysts, not a suspected torsion where delay risks ovarian necrosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CA 125 helps evaluate postmenopausal masses for cancer and would not change the urgent management of torsion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Oral contraceptives address irregular menses and androgen excess in PMOS; they have no role in acute torsion.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Bilateral oophorectomy with hysterectomy is reserved for cancer; torsion in a reproductive-age woman calls for ovary-sparing detorsion.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old woman, 11 years postmenopausal, is found on bimanual examination to have a left adnexal mass. She is otherwise asymptomatic. Which of the following is the most appropriate first test?

explanation.summary: Pelvic ultrasound is the first test for any patient with a pelvic mass because it distinguishes cystic from solid tissue.
explanation.whyCorrect: All pelvic masses are initially evaluated with pelvic ultrasound, which is good for distinguishing cysts from solid tissue. This matters especially in a postmenopausal patient, who should not have functional cysts and in whom ovarian cancer is part of the differential.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Diagnostic laparoscopy for tissue diagnosis is reserved for selected patients depending on the size and appearance seen on imaging, which comes first.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hemoglobin A1c screens for diabetes in the PMOS workup, not the evaluation of a postmenopausal adnexal mass.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Prolactin is checked when PMOS-like endocrine disorders are being excluded, not as the first test for a pelvic mass.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pregnancy testing is indicated for amenorrhea in reproductive-age patients, not an 11-years-postmenopausal woman.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old postmenopausal woman with an ovarian cyst has an elevated serum CA 125 level. Her physician cautions that this result alone does not prove ovarian cancer. Which of the following conditions is a recognized cause of a falsely elevated CA 125?

explanation.summary: CA 125 is nonspecific: endometriosis, uterine leiomyomas, pregnancy, and liver or kidney failure can all elevate it without ovarian malignancy.
explanation.whyCorrect: CA 125 is elevated in 50%-85% of ovarian cancers but also in 5%-10% of patients without ovarian malignancy. Recognized non-malignant causes include endometriosis, uterine leiomyomas, pregnancy, and liver or kidney failure, and the false-positive rate is especially high in premenopausal patients.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Hypothyroidism can alter the ovulatory cycle and cause functional cysts, but it is not listed as a cause of elevated CA 125.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Obstructive sleep apnea accompanies obesity in PMOS and does not raise CA 125.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Type 2 diabetes is part of the metabolic syndrome associated with PMOS, not a cause of CA 125 elevation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Acanthosis nigricans is a skin finding of insulin resistance and certain cancers, not a listed cause of elevated CA 125.

questions.stem: A female neonate undergoing abdominal imaging for an unrelated indication is incidentally found to have a small ovarian cyst. Which of the following best explains its development and expected course?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Maternal estrogen stimulated follicular growth; it will resolve as that estrogen is withdrawn

choices.label: B
choices.text: Neonatal ovulation formed a corpus luteum; it will persist until menarche

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ectopic endometrial implants bled into the ovary; surgical excision is required

choices.label: D
choices.text: A germ cell neoplasm is developing; urgent oophorectomy is indicated

choices.label: E
choices.text: Excess neonatal LH stimulated theca cells; antiandrogen therapy is needed

explanation.summary: Fetal and neonatal ovarian cysts arise from high maternal estrogen stimulating follicular growth and usually resolve without intervention once maternal estrogen is withdrawn.
explanation.whyCorrect: Babies do not ovulate, but high levels of maternal estrogen can stimulate follicular growth, occasionally producing a functional cyst found incidentally in a fetus or neonate. The cyst usually resolves without intervention as maternal estrogen is withdrawn, just as some newborns have transient uterine bleeding from the same in utero stimulation.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Neonates do not ovulate, so a corpus luteum cannot be the source.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Endometriomas occur when endometriosis forms on the ovaries in menstruating patients, not neonates, and this cyst needs no excision.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neoplastic cysts are suspected chiefly in postmenopausal patients; an incidental neonatal cyst is expected to resolve.
whyWrongByChoice.E: LH-driven theca stimulation is the mechanism of PMOS in reproductive-age females, and no antiandrogen therapy is indicated here.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old woman presents with irregular menses, acne, and coarse hair on her chin and lower abdomen. Her BMI is 34 kg/m2 and she has velvety hyperpigmented plaques on her neck. Ultrasound shows numerous small follicles arranged around the periphery of both ovaries. Increased secretion of which of the following hormones is the initiating step in the pathogenesis of her ovarian androgen excess?

explanation.summary: In PMOS, an exaggerated LH response to GnRH raises LH, which stimulates ovarian theca interna cells to produce androstenedione, the key hormonal finding of focal ovarian hyperandrogenism.
explanation.whyCorrect: This patient has PMOS: hirsutism, acne, irregular menses, obesity, acanthosis nigricans, and a string-of-pearls ovary. Elevated anterior pituitary LH secretion, from an exaggerated response to GnRH, stimulates theca interna cells to increase androstenedione production, causing hyperandrogenism and some degree of hyperthecosis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: FSH is suppressed in PMOS because elevated estrone inhibits pituitary FSH secretion, raising the LH/FSH ratio.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Progesterone is low in PMOS since anovulation means no corpus luteum forms to produce it.
whyWrongByChoice.D: hCG drives theca lutein cysts in placental disorders like hydatidiform mole, not PMOS.
whyWrongByChoice.E: TSH is measured to exclude thyroid disease that mimics PMOS, not as a driver of ovarian androgen excess.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman with longstanding PMOS, obesity, and chronic anovulation asks about her long-term health risks. Which of the following malignancies is she at increased risk of developing, and by what mechanism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Endometrial carcinoma, from estrogen unopposed by progesterone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ovarian carcinoma, from repeated follicular rupture

choices.label: C
choices.text: Breast carcinoma, from chronic progesterone excess

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cervical carcinoma, from chronic androgen exposure

explanation.summary: PMOS causes high estrogen with low progesterone, and this unopposed estrogen is a risk factor for endometrial hyperplasia and endometrial carcinoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: Women with PMOS are not ovulating regularly, so no corpus luteum forms and progesterone stays low, while adipose tissue aromatizes androgens to estrone, raising estrogen. Estrogen unopposed by progesterone drives endometrial hyperplasia and increases the risk of endometrial carcinoma.

whyWrongByChoice.B: PMOS follicles are arrested and unruptured; the lecture links PMOS risk to the endometrium, not the ovary.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Progesterone is low, not excessive, in PMOS because of anovulation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cervical cancer is not the malignancy the lecture associates with PMOS, and androgens are not described as its driver.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Choriocarcinoma is a placental disorder that causes theca lutein cysts; it is not a consequence of PMOS.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman with PMOS has been unable to conceive for two years because of anovulation. She is prescribed a drug that acts as a mixed agonist-antagonist at the estrogen receptor and is warned about pelvic pain and hot flashes. This same drug class is sometimes used in males for which of the following purposes?

explanation.summary: Clomiphene, a SERM, restores ovulation in anovulatory PMOS patients and is sometimes used in males to treat gynecomastia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Clomiphene is a mixed agonist-antagonist of the estrogen receptor, a selective estrogen receptor modulator. It helps anovulatory women with PMOS regain fertility, its adverse effects include pelvic pain and hot flashes, and it is sometimes used in males to treat gynecomastia.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Male-pattern hair growth in PMOS (hirsutism) is treated with antiandrogens like spironolactone, not SERMs, and is a finding in females.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The lecture does not describe SERMs as prostate cancer therapy; prostate cancer appears only as a cause of acanthosis nigricans.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Insulin resistance in PMOS is addressed with weight management and diabetes care, not clomiphene.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Torsion management is urgent surgical detorsion; SERMs play no role, and this indication is invented.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old woman has a complex 8-cm ovarian cyst with features on ultrasound that raise strong suspicion for malignancy. Surgical removal is planned. Which of the following is the main reason an open approach is preferred over laparoscopy in this setting?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rupture of the cyst and spread of tumor cells are less likely

choices.label: B
choices.text: Open surgery allows the cyst to be observed with serial imaging

choices.label: C
choices.text: Laparoscopy cannot distinguish cystic from solid tissue

choices.label: D
choices.text: Open surgery avoids the need for any tissue diagnosis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Laparoscopy is contraindicated in postmenopausal patients

explanation.summary: Open surgery is favored for suspected malignancy because cyst rupture and subsequent spread of tumor cells are less likely than with laparoscopy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Persistent, symptomatic, or enlarging cysts are removed by laparoscopy or open surgery depending on the preoperative suspicion of malignancy. When cancer is suspected, open surgery is more commonly used because rupture of the cyst contents and subsequent spread of tumor cells are less likely with this approach.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Serial ultrasound observation is the conservative alternative to surgery, not a feature of the open approach.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Distinguishing cystic from solid tissue is the job of pelvic ultrasound, and it is not the reason to choose open over laparoscopic surgery.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tissue diagnosis remains essential in suspected cancer; the approach does not eliminate that need.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Laparoscopy is used in postmenopausal patients when malignancy suspicion is low; there is no such contraindication.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old woman who went through menopause at age 51 is found on pelvic ultrasound to have a 4-cm simple-appearing ovarian cyst. Her physician explains that this finding deserves more concern than the identical finding in a 25-year-old. Which of the following best explains why?

choices.label: A
choices.text: She is no longer ovulating, so functional cysts are not expected

choices.label: B
choices.text: Her ovaries secrete more estrogen than they did before menopause

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cysts are far more likely to rupture after menopause

choices.label: D
choices.text: Her granulosa cells respond more strongly to circulating FSH

choices.label: E
choices.text: Endometriosis deposits on the ovary are more common after menopause

explanation.summary: Functional cysts are consequences of the ovulatory cycle, so a cyst in a postmenopausal patient raises concern for a neoplastic lesion.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ovarian cancer is always part of the differential for an ovarian cyst, particularly in postmenopausal patients. Because these patients are not ovulating, they should not have functional cysts, and a cyst found in them should raise suspicion for a neoplastic lesion.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The lecture ties cyst-related estrogen to the granulosa cells of cycling follicles; a postmenopausal ovary is not driving an ovulatory cycle.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Rupture is a complication of ovarian cysts generally; the lecture does not describe it as a specific postmenopausal concern.
whyWrongByChoice.D: FSH-driven follicular estrogen production belongs to the menstruating female, in whom cysts are most common.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Endometriomas form when ectopic endometrial tissue on the ovary bleeds in menstruating patients; that is not the concern here.

questions.stem: A 46-year-old woman who is still menstruating has been taking tamoxifen since completing treatment for breast cancer. Pelvic ultrasound obtained for mild pelvic pressure shows a 3-cm simple, fluid-filled left ovarian cyst. Which of the following best explains this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An antiestrogen drug has altered her ovulatory cycle

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ectopic endometrial tissue has implanted on the ovary

choices.label: C
choices.text: Elevated hCG has stimulated the theca lutein layer

choices.label: D
choices.text: Metastatic breast carcinoma has seeded the ovary

choices.label: E
choices.text: An exaggerated LH response to GnRH has raised androgens

explanation.summary: Drugs and conditions that alter the ovulatory cycle, including antiestrogens such as tamoxifen, can produce functional ovarian cysts.
explanation.whyCorrect: Functional cysts are consequences of the normal ovulatory cycle, and anything that perturbs that cycle can generate one. The lecture specifically lists antiestrogen drugs (tamoxifen), infertility treatments, pregnancy, and hypothyroidism as causes of functional cysts.

whyWrongByChoice.B: An endometrioma contains old brown-black blood and causes pain that peaks with menstruation, not a simple fluid-filled cyst.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Theca lutein cysts require the high hCG of placental disorders such as hydatidiform mole or choriocarcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The lecture attributes cysts in this setting to the drug's effect on ovulation, not to metastatic seeding.
whyWrongByChoice.E: An exaggerated LH response to GnRH is the pathogenesis of PMOS, which produces numerous small bilateral follicles rather than one simple cyst.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old woman has had several months of anovulatory cycles. Ultrasound shows a single 3.5-cm thin-walled right ovarian cyst; the left ovary appears normal. Which of the following best describes how this lesion most likely formed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A follicle failed to rupture and the ovum remained in the ovary

choices.label: B
choices.text: The central cavity of the corpus luteum persisted after ovulation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Endometrial tissue implanted on the ovarian surface and bled

choices.label: D
choices.text: Circulating hCG stimulated the theca lutein layer to expand

choices.label: E
choices.text: Arrested subcortical follicles accumulated around both ovaries

explanation.summary: Follicular cysts arise from an unruptured follicle in an anovulatory cycle, or from degeneration of the egg follicle after rupture.
explanation.whyCorrect: Follicular cysts are the most common ovarian cyst. They arise either from an unruptured follicle due to anovulation, in which the ovum remains in the ovary, or from degeneration of the egg follicle after rupture. This patient's anovulatory cycles and single thin-walled cyst fit the first mechanism.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Persistence of the corpus luteum's central cavity produces a corpus luteum cyst, which requires that ovulation have occurred.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Endometrial implants on the ovary form an endometrioma, a chocolate cyst filled with old blood rather than a thin-walled clear cyst.
whyWrongByChoice.D: hCG-driven theca lutein cysts accompany placental disorders and are typically bilateral and multiple.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Arrested peripheral subcortical follicles describe PMOS ovaries, which are bilaterally involved with follicles smaller than functional cysts.

questions.stem: A cystectomy specimen from a 28-year-old woman contains a 4-cm thin-walled cyst with a smooth external surface filled with clear, straw-colored fluid. Microscopically the wall is lined by granulosa cells with an outer rim of luteinized theca cells. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: A thin-walled, smooth-surfaced cyst with clear to straw-colored fluid lined by granulosa and luteinized theca cells is a follicular cyst.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture describes the follicular cyst as a thin-walled cyst with a smooth external surface measuring more than 3 cm and filled with clear to straw-colored fluid, whose wall is made up of theca and granulosa cells. This specimen matches that description exactly.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A corpus luteum cyst has a yellow, convoluted wall with undulating contours and marked luteinization giving a pink hue, not clear fluid in a thin smooth wall.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An endometrioma is filled with thick old blood broken down to hemosiderin, producing brown to black contents.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Theca lutein cysts arise from hCG stimulation in placental disorders and are usually multiple and bilateral.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Teratomas are neoplastic cysts arising with ovarian tumors, not lesions lined by granulosa and theca cells.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman has a follicular ovarian cyst, and her serum estrogen level is at the upper limit of normal. The granulosa cells lining the wall of her cyst are producing this estrogen in response to which of the following?

explanation.summary: Most ovarian cysts arise from normal ovarian structures, and the theca and granulosa cells of the follicle make estrogen in response to FSH.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture states that most ovarian cysts arise from normal ovarian structures, specifically the follicle and its theca and granulosa cells, which make estrogen in response to follicle stimulating hormone. The granulosa cells lining a follicular cyst continue that estrogen production, which can cause menstrual irregularity.

whyWrongByChoice.B: hCG acts on the theca lutein layer of the corpus luteum to form theca lutein cysts, and those cells make androstenedione rather than estrogen.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Progesterone is the product of luteinized theca cells in a corpus luteum cyst, not the stimulus for granulosa estrogen production.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Androstenedione is an androgen precursor made by theca cells; it is not a pituitary stimulus to the granulosa cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: TSH is checked when excluding endocrine mimics of PMOS and does not drive granulosa cell estrogen production.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman undergoes laparoscopy for suspected ovarian torsion. The right ovary and fallopian tube are twisted around the vascular pedicle, and the ovary is enlarged and dusky. Which of the following best describes the sequence of events producing this appearance?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Venous outflow obstruction with congestion, then ischemia and necrosis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Arterial occlusion with immediate infarction before any venous congestion

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hemorrhage into the cyst, then rupture with intraperitoneal bleeding

choices.label: D
choices.text: Bacterial infection of the cyst, then abscess formation and ischemia

choices.label: E
choices.text: Endometriotic adhesions tethering the ovary, then progressive infarction

explanation.summary: Torsion of the ovary around its vascular pedicle causes venous congestion first, then ischemia and possible necrosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ovarian torsion is twisting of the ovary, often with the fallopian tube, around its vascular pedicle, leading to venous congestion, ischemia, and possible necrosis. The congested, enlarged, dusky ovary reflects obstructed venous outflow before arterial inflow fails, which is why urgent detorsion can still preserve the ovary.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Arterial flow can persist initially, which is why normal Doppler flow does not exclude torsion; congestion precedes frank infarction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hemorrhage with rupture and intraperitoneal bleeding is a separate cyst complication and does not involve twisting of the pedicle.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Infection is a feared consequence of necrosis, not the initiating mechanism of the ischemic changes in torsion.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Endometriosis forms endometriomas on the ovary; the lecture attributes torsion to twisting around the vascular pedicle, commonly with a mass over 5 cm.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman undergoing ovulation induction for infertility has a 6-cm right ovarian cyst and intermittent right pelvic pain. Her physician counsels her about the risk of ovarian torsion. Which of the following additional circumstances would further increase that risk?

explanation.summary: Risk factors for ovarian torsion include ovarian masses or cysts larger than 5 cm, pregnancy, ovulation induction, and prior torsion.
explanation.whyCorrect: Torsion most commonly affects reproductive-age females and is strongly associated with ovarian masses or cysts over 5 cm. The lecture lists pregnancy, ovulation induction, and prior torsion as additional risk factors, so a pregnancy resulting from her treatment would add to the risk she already carries.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Oral contraceptives are used in PMOS for cycle regulation and androgen excess; they are not listed as a torsion risk factor.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CA 125 is a nonspecific marker used mainly to help evaluate postmenopausal masses for malignancy, not a determinant of torsion risk.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hypothyroidism is listed as a cause of functional cysts, not as a risk factor for torsion.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Torsion most commonly affects reproductive-age females, so menopause does not add risk.

questions.stem: A 44-year-old woman is evaluated for a newly discovered pelvic mass. A complete medical history is obtained. Which of the following elements of her history would most increase her risk of ovarian cancer?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ten years of combined oral contraceptive use

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uterine leiomyomas seen on prior imaging

explanation.summary: Family history of ovarian cancer, infertility, and endometriosis all increase a patient's risk of ovarian cancer.
explanation.whyCorrect: Much of the history taken in a patient with a pelvic mass is aimed at gauging ovarian cancer risk. The lecture identifies a family history of ovarian cancer, infertility, and endometriosis as data points that increase that risk, so longstanding endometriosis is the answer here.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A hydatidiform mole causes hCG-driven theca lutein cysts that recede as hCG falls; it is not given as an ovarian cancer risk factor.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Oral contraceptives are discussed as PMOS therapy; the lecture does not list them among ovarian cancer risk factors.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hypothyroidism is a cause of functional cysts, not a risk factor for ovarian malignancy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Uterine leiomyomas are a cause of a falsely elevated CA 125, not a risk factor for ovarian cancer.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old woman with obesity, acne, and coarse facial hair has had no menstrual period for 4 months. PMOS is suspected. Which of the following must be excluded first in the evaluation of her amenorrhea?

explanation.summary: Any patient presenting with amenorrhea should have pregnancy ruled out before the rest of the PMOS evaluation proceeds.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture is explicit that patients presenting with amenorrhea should have pregnancy ruled out. Only after that do the other components of the PMOS evaluation, such as hemoglobin A1c and hormonal testing, become relevant.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Hemoglobin A1c is measured because of the high incidence of diabetes in PMOS, but diabetes is not the first thing excluded in amenorrhea.
whyWrongByChoice.C: TSH is part of the evaluation for endocrine mimics of PMOS, but it comes after pregnancy has been excluded.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Prolactin is checked because other endocrine abnormalities resemble PMOS, again after a pregnancy test.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Serum cortisol is considered only if signs or symptoms suggest Cushing syndrome, not as the first exclusion.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old postmenopausal woman has a 7-cm adnexal mass with solid components and internal septations on pelvic ultrasound. Her serum CA 125 level is within the reference range. Which of the following is the most appropriate interpretation of this result?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ovarian cancer remains possible despite the normal CA 125

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ovarian malignancy is effectively excluded by this result

choices.label: C
choices.text: The normal result confirms that this is a functional cyst

choices.label: D
choices.text: CA 125 would be more accurate if she were premenopausal

choices.label: E
choices.text: The normal result excludes endometriosis as the cause

explanation.summary: Only 50%-85% of patients with ovarian cancer have an elevated CA 125, so a normal level does not exclude malignancy.
explanation.whyCorrect: CA 125 is tested in postmenopausal patients to help rule out ovarian cancer, but 50%-85% of those with ovarian cancer have an elevated level, which means a substantial fraction do not. A normal value therefore cannot exclude malignancy in a postmenopausal patient with a suspicious mass, and further evaluation is still required.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A normal CA 125 cannot exclude cancer when a sizeable minority of ovarian cancers never raise the marker.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Postmenopausal patients are not ovulating and should not have functional cysts, and CA 125 does not establish that diagnosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The opposite is true: a high false-positive rate is seen in premenopausal patients, which is why the test is used mainly after menopause.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Endometriosis is a cause of an elevated CA 125, so a normal value neither confirms nor excludes it here.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman has a 7-cm ovarian cyst whose size and appearance on pelvic ultrasound remain indeterminate. Which of the following would provide a definitive tissue diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Depending on a cyst's size and appearance, diagnostic laparoscopy is used to obtain a definitive tissue diagnosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pelvic ultrasound is the first test for any pelvic mass because it distinguishes cystic from solid tissue, but it does not yield tissue. Depending on the size and appearance of the lesion, some patients undergo diagnostic laparoscopy for a definitive tissue diagnosis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Serial ultrasound is the conservative management strategy for most cysts; it monitors rather than diagnoses tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.C: There are no good blood tests for ovarian cysts, and CA 125 is nonspecific with a high false-positive rate.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hemoglobin A1c assesses glucose intolerance in the PMOS workup and says nothing about the cyst.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Testosterone and prolactin are used to evaluate endocrine disorders that mimic PMOS, not to diagnose an ovarian cyst.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman undergoing CT for suspected nephrolithiasis is incidentally noted to have a 3.5-cm simple right ovarian cyst. She has regular menses and no pelvic symptoms, and pelvic ultrasound confirms a simple fluid-filled cyst. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Open surgical removal of the cyst

choices.label: E
choices.text: Clomiphene to suppress further cyst formation

explanation.summary: Management of ovarian cysts is often conservative, and most are simply observed with serial ultrasounds.
explanation.whyCorrect: Most ovarian cysts require no treatment. Management is often conservative, with observation by serial ultrasounds, and a simple cyst found incidentally in a menstruating woman is most likely a functional cyst that will resolve on its own.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Surgical removal is reserved for persistent, symptomatic, or enlarging cysts, none of which she has.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Open surgery is chosen chiefly when malignancy is suspected, because cyst rupture and tumor spread are less likely with that approach.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Bilateral oophorectomy with or without hysterectomy is reserved for patients with cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Clomiphene is used to restore ovulation in infertile patients with PMOS and has no role in suppressing cysts.

questions.stem: A 37-year-old woman with a simple ovarian cyst has been followed conservatively with ultrasound. Which of the following findings would most strongly indicate surgical removal rather than continued observation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Progressive enlargement of the cyst on repeat imaging

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clear straw-colored fluid seen within the cyst

choices.label: C
choices.text: A thin smooth wall without internal septations

choices.label: D
choices.text: Resolution of her mild intermittent bloating

choices.label: E
choices.text: A CA 125 level within the reference range

explanation.summary: Persistent, symptomatic, or enlarging ovarian cysts are removed surgically; the rest are observed.
explanation.whyCorrect: Most cysts are managed conservatively with serial ultrasounds. The lecture identifies three triggers for surgical removal by laparoscopy or open surgery: cysts that persist, cysts that cause symptoms, and cysts that enlarge. Progressive enlargement is therefore the finding that changes management.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Clear straw-colored fluid is the expected content of a benign follicular cyst and is reassuring.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A thin smooth wall is the appearance of a simple functional cyst, which supports continued observation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Resolving symptoms argue for continued observation, since symptomatic cysts are the ones taken to surgery.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A normal CA 125 does not by itself mandate surgery, and the marker is nonspecific in any case.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman with irregular menses, acne, and hirsutism is diagnosed with polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS). Which of the following statements about this disorder is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is the most common cause of infertility in females

choices.label: B
choices.text: It affects fewer than 1% of reproductive-age females

choices.label: C
choices.text: It usually first becomes apparent after menopause

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is the most common cause of postmenopausal bleeding

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is most often diagnosed in the sixth decade of life

explanation.summary: PMOS is the most common hormonal disorder of reproductive-age females, affects 5%-10% of them, and is the leading cause of female infertility.
explanation.whyCorrect: PMOS, formerly called polycystic ovarian syndrome, is the most common hormonal disorder among females of reproductive age, affecting 5%-10% of the female population. It is also the most common cause of infertility in females and frequently becomes manifest during adolescence.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The prevalence is 5%-10% of the female population, far above 1%.
whyWrongByChoice.C: PMOS frequently becomes manifest during adolescence, not after menopause.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The lecture links PMOS to endometrial hyperplasia and carcinoma through unopposed estrogen, but does not name it the leading cause of postmenopausal bleeding.
whyWrongByChoice.E: It is a disorder of females of reproductive age, often recognized in adolescence.

questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman with longstanding PMOS undergoes hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy for endometrial carcinoma. Which of the following best describes the expected gross appearance of her ovaries?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bilaterally enlarged, smooth-surfaced, with multiple subcortical follicles

choices.label: B
choices.text: One enlarged ovary with a single cyst of clear straw-colored fluid

choices.label: C
choices.text: One enlarged ovary with a yellow, convoluted cyst wall

choices.label: D
choices.text: One enlarged ovary with a cavity of thick brown-black material

choices.label: E
choices.text: Bilaterally enlarged ovaries with cysts that recede as hCG falls

explanation.summary: Polycystic ovaries in PMOS are bilaterally enlarged with a smooth external surface; the 'cysts' are multiple arrested subcortical follicles rather than true cysts.
explanation.whyCorrect: Grossly, polycystic ovaries are bilaterally enlarged with a smooth external surface and no obvious surface cysts. Despite the name, the cysts of PMOS are not true cysts but multiple arrested subcortical follicles, visible on cross-section and responsible for the peripheral string-of-pearls ultrasound appearance.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A single thin-walled cyst with clear to straw-colored fluid is a follicular cyst, which is larger than the follicles of PMOS.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A yellow, convoluted cyst wall describes a corpus luteum cyst, a functional cyst of an ovulatory cycle.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Thick brown-black contents identify an endometrioma, the chocolate cyst of ovarian endometriosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Bilateral cysts that recede as hCG falls are theca lutein cysts driven by placental disorders.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman with PMOS has an elevated LH/FSH ratio on laboratory testing, and ultrasound shows numerous small follicles arranged around the periphery of both ovaries. Which of the following best explains why these follicles have accumulated?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The LH/FSH imbalance prevents follicles from maturing and rupturing

choices.label: B
choices.text: High progesterone maintains follicles beyond their normal lifespan

choices.label: C
choices.text: hCG stimulates the theca lutein layer to form multiple cysts

choices.label: D
choices.text: Follicles degenerate after ovulation and fill with clear fluid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ectopic endometrial tissue forms multiple implants on the ovary

explanation.summary: In PMOS, estrone-driven FSH suppression raises the LH/FSH ratio, and that imbalance inhibits follicle maturation, leaving many unruptured follicles.
explanation.whyCorrect: Peripheral aromatization of androstenedione to estrone raises estrone, which inhibits pituitary FSH secretion and elevates the LH/FSH ratio. That imbalance inhibits follicle maturation, so multiple unruptured follicles accumulate and produce the many ovarian 'cysts' of PMOS. The same imbalance is a likely cause of the impaired ovulation and infertility.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Progesterone is low in PMOS because anovulation means no corpus luteum forms to secrete it.
whyWrongByChoice.C: hCG stimulation of the theca lutein layer produces theca lutein cysts in placental disorders, not the arrested follicles of PMOS.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Degeneration of the follicle after rupture is one route to a follicular cyst, but the PMOS follicles never rupture.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ovarian endometrial implants create an endometrioma filled with old blood, a different disease entirely.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman with PMOS has a BMI of 38 kg/m2 and an elevated serum estrone level. Which of the following best explains this laboratory finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adipose tissue aromatizes androstenedione to estrone

choices.label: B
choices.text: The corpus luteum secretes estrone during the luteal phase

choices.label: C
choices.text: Elevated FSH drives granulosa cells to secrete estrone

choices.label: D
choices.text: hCG stimulates the theca lutein layer to secrete estrone

choices.label: E
choices.text: The adrenal cortex secretes estrone in response to cortisol

explanation.summary: Peripheral adipose tissue aromatizes the excess androstenedione of PMOS into estrone, which is why PMOS and obesity are linked.
explanation.whyCorrect: High LH stimulates ovarian theca interna cells to make androstenedione. Peripheral adipose tissue aromatizes that androstenedione to estrone, which explains the connection between PMOS and obesity and why an obese patient has a higher estrone level. The resulting estrone then inhibits pituitary FSH secretion.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Patients with PMOS are anovulatory, so no corpus luteum forms to secrete hormones.
whyWrongByChoice.C: FSH is suppressed, not elevated, in PMOS because of estrone's inhibitory effect on the pituitary.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The theca lutein layer responds to hCG in placental disorders and makes androstenedione, not estrone.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The lecture locates aromatization of androgens to estrogen in peripheral adipose tissue, not in the adrenal cortex.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman with PMOS has laboratory studies showing high androgen and high estrogen levels with a low progesterone level. Which of the following best explains the low progesterone?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anovulation means no corpus luteum forms to make it

choices.label: B
choices.text: Adipose tissue aromatizes progesterone into estrone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Elevated LH directly suppresses its release by the ovary

choices.label: D
choices.text: Granulosa cell estrogen inhibits its secretion by the theca

choices.label: E
choices.text: Insulin resistance blocks the final step of its synthesis

explanation.summary: Because females with PMOS do not ovulate regularly, no corpus luteum forms and progesterone stays low, leaving estrogen unopposed.
explanation.whyCorrect: High androgen, high estrogen, and low progesterone levels are present in PMOS. Females with PMOS aren't ovulating regularly, so there is no progesterone production from the corpus luteum. That unopposed estrogen is what puts them at risk for endometrial hyperplasia and carcinoma.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Adipose aromatization converts androstenedione to estrone; progesterone is not the substrate.
whyWrongByChoice.C: High LH in PMOS acts on theca interna cells to raise androstenedione; the lecture does not describe it suppressing progesterone directly.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The lecture attributes low progesterone to the absence of a corpus luteum, not to estrogen feedback on theca cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Insulin resistance is part of the metabolic picture of PMOS but is not described as blocking progesterone synthesis.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman with regular prior menses, a normal BMI, and no hirsutism develops velvety hyperpigmented plaques on her neck and axillae over 3 months, along with 10 kg of unintentional weight loss. Which of the following is most likely responsible for her skin finding?

explanation.summary: Acanthosis nigricans accompanies PMOS but is also seen with hypocortisolism, hypothyroidism, Cushing disease, oral contraceptive or corticosteroid use, and cancers of the prostate, breast, ovaries, and stomach.
explanation.whyCorrect: Acanthosis nigricans is a velvety hyperpigmented plaque on the neck, axillae, or below the breasts or elbows. Beyond PMOS, the lecture lists stomach cancer among its associated malignancies, and rapid onset with weight loss in a woman without PMOS features points to that malignant association.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Colorectal cancer is not among the malignancies the lecture associates with acanthosis nigricans.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hypothyroidism, not hyperthyroidism, is the thyroid disorder listed with acanthosis nigricans.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hyperparathyroidism is not among the listed causes of this skin finding.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Kidney failure is given as a cause of an elevated CA 125, not of acanthosis nigricans.

questions.stem: A 15-year-old girl who reached menarche 2 years ago has cycles occurring every 5 to 8 weeks and mild facial acne. Her BMI is normal and she has no hirsutism or clitoral enlargement. Which of the following best characterizes her evaluation for PMOS?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Her acne and cycle irregularity are nonspecific at this age

choices.label: B
choices.text: Her irregular cycles alone establish the diagnosis of PMOS

choices.label: C
choices.text: Her acne is sufficient evidence of clinical hyperandrogenism

choices.label: D
choices.text: Absence of hirsutism reliably excludes PMOS in adolescents

choices.label: E
choices.text: PMOS cannot become manifest until after age 20 years

explanation.summary: PMOS is harder to diagnose in adolescence, where anovulatory cycles and acne are common and hirsutism is still developing; diagnosis rests on a persistent abnormal menstrual pattern or evidence of hyperandrogenism.
explanation.whyCorrect: Anovulatory cycles and menstrual irregularity are frequent in adolescents, and signs of hyperandrogenism are less reliable because hirsutism is still in a developmental phase and acne is common at this age. PMOS can be suggested by a persistent abnormal menstrual pattern or clinical and/or biochemical evidence of hyperandrogenism, so her current findings are not yet diagnostic.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Menstrual irregularity is frequent in adolescents, so by itself it cannot establish the diagnosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Acne is common in adolescence and is an unreliable indicator of hyperandrogenism at this age.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hirsutism is still developing in adolescents, so its absence does not exclude PMOS.
whyWrongByChoice.E: PMOS frequently becomes manifest during adolescence, which is precisely why the diagnosis is difficult here.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman being evaluated for suspected PMOS has irregular menses and hirsutism. She also reports that her shoe and ring sizes have increased over the past 2 years and that her facial features have coarsened.
