In addition to the standard evaluation, which of the following tests is most appropriate?

explanation.summary: Because PMOS resembles other endocrine disorders, additional tests are chosen by the signs present: insulin-like growth factor 1 when acromegaly is suggested.
explanation.whyCorrect: The standard PMOS evaluation includes TSH, prolactin, and testosterone, and other endocrine tests are added when signs or symptoms suggest a specific alternative. Enlarging hands and feet with coarsening facial features suggest acromegaly, for which the lecture names insulin-like growth factor 1.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Serum cortisol is the test added when Cushing syndrome is suspected, and her features point to acromegaly instead.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CA 125 is used to help evaluate a pelvic mass for malignancy, chiefly in postmenopausal patients.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A pregnancy test is indicated for amenorrhea; her problem is irregular menses with acromegalic features.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Androstenedione is the androgen produced by theca cells in PMOS, but measuring it would not address her acromegalic features.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman with PMOS has taken combined oral contraceptives for 8 months. Her cycles are now regular, but coarse hair on her face and chin persists and bothers her. She does not wish to conceive. Which of the following is the most appropriate addition to her regimen?

explanation.summary: Hirsutism in PMOS is treated with antiandrogen therapy such as spironolactone or eplerenone, typically added to oral contraceptives and with appropriate contraception in place.
explanation.whyCorrect: Combined oral contraceptives address irregular menses and reduce androgen excess, but persistent hirsutism is treated with antiandrogen therapy such as spironolactone or eplerenone. These agents are used as an adjunct to oral contraceptives and require appropriate contraception, both of which are satisfied here.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Clomiphene is used to restore ovulation in patients with PMOS who want to conceive, and she does not.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tamoxifen is named as an antiestrogen that can cause functional ovarian cysts, not as therapy for hirsutism.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Levothyroxine would treat hypothyroidism, which is excluded during the PMOS evaluation, not hirsutism.
whyWrongByChoice.E: hCG drives theca lutein cysts in placental disorders and has no role in treating hirsutism.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman with PMOS reports menstrual periods occurring every 2 to 4 months and worsening acne. She is sexually active and is not attempting pregnancy. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial pharmacologic therapy?

explanation.summary: Patients with PMOS and irregular menses are treated with combined oral contraceptives, which also help reduce androgen excess.
explanation.whyCorrect: Treatment of PMOS targets its associated abnormalities. Patients with irregular menses are treated with combined oral contraceptives, which have the added benefit of reducing androgen excess and therefore the acne and hirsutism that come with it.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Clomiphene is used to regain fertility in females who do not ovulate, and she is not trying to conceive.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Antiandrogens such as eplerenone are used typically as an adjunct to oral contraceptives, not as first-line monotherapy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Laparoscopy is for definitive tissue diagnosis of a pelvic mass, not for medical management of PMOS.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Bilateral oophorectomy is reserved for patients with cancer, not for PMOS.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman with PMOS and a BMI of 36 kg/m2 reports urinating far more frequently than usual over the past several months, along with fatigue. Her urine pregnancy test is negative. Which of the following tests best evaluates the most likely cause of her urinary frequency?

explanation.summary: Frequent urination in PMOS reflects diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia, and hemoglobin A1c is measured because of the high incidence of diabetes in these patients.
explanation.whyCorrect: PMOS is typically seen in females with metabolic syndrome, including obesity, insulin resistance, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Frequent urination in these patients is attributed to diabetes mellitus and hyperglycemia, and because of the high incidence of diabetes a hemoglobin A1c is measured to assess for glucose intolerance or frank diabetes.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Prolactin is checked to exclude endocrine disorders that mimic PMOS, not to explain polyuria.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CA 125 helps evaluate a pelvic mass for malignancy and has nothing to do with urinary frequency.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Testosterone documents hyperandrogenism, which underlies hirsutism and acne rather than polyuria.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pelvic ultrasound shows the peripheral follicles of PMOS but would not explain her urinary symptoms.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old woman presents with 3 months of bloating, early satiety, and pelvic discomfort. Examination reveals abdominal distention with a fluid wave and a fixed right adnexal mass. Serum CA-125 is markedly elevated. After debulking surgery, histology of the ovarian mass shows invasive epithelial nests with high-grade nuclear atypia and numerous concentric, laminated calcified spheres. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Psammoma bodies with high-grade atypia, ascites, and elevated CA-125 point to high-grade serous carcinoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: Serous carcinomas are the most common malignant ovarian tumors and are histologically noted for psammoma bodies, concentric layers of calcium. High-grade serous carcinoma classically presents in older women with peritoneal spread, ascites, and elevated CA-125.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Mucinous carcinoma forms large mucin-filled multiloculated cysts and secretes CEA; psammoma bodies are not its hallmark.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Endometrioid carcinoma shows back-to-back malignant glands resembling endometrial tissue, not laminated calcifications.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Clear cell carcinoma is composed of large cells with abundant clear cytoplasm forming sheets or tubes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Brenner tumors contain nests of urothelium-like epithelium and are usually benign.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman with a known germline BRCA1 mutation is diagnosed with an invasive ovarian carcinoma showing marked cytologic atypia. Molecular analysis of the tumor is most likely to reveal a mutation in which of the following genes?

explanation.summary: Ovarian carcinomas in BRCA1/2 carriers are almost always high-grade serous carcinomas with TP53 mutations.
explanation.whyCorrect: High-grade serous carcinoma arises from in situ lesions in the fallopian tube fimbriae and is associated with TP53 mutations. Almost all ovarian carcinomas arising in women with BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations are high-grade serous carcinomas carrying TP53 mutations.

whyWrongByChoice.A: KRAS mutations characterize low-grade serous and mucinous tumors, not BRCA-associated high-grade disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: BRAF mutations are found in serous borderline tumors and low-grade serous carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: RET is not a mutation described in ovarian epithelial carcinogenesis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: APC is not part of the described pathogenesis of ovarian epithelial tumors.

questions.stem: A 44-year-old woman undergoes staging surgery for a cystic ovarian mass lined by complex branching papillae with mildly atypical, ciliated cuboidal cells, low mitotic activity, and no stromal invasion. Staging shows disease confined to the ovary. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

explanation.summary: Serous borderline tumors confined to the ovary are managed surgically without adjuvant therapy.
explanation.whyCorrect: The histology describes a serous borderline tumor: epithelial proliferation with branching papillae but no stromal invasion. Management is primarily surgical, and there is currently no indication for adjuvant chemotherapy or radiation when disease is confined to the ovary or limited to noninvasive extraovarian implants.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Platinum-based chemotherapy is used for invasive serous carcinoma, not borderline tumors confined to the ovary.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Radiation has no indication for borderline tumors confined to the ovary.
whyWrongByChoice.C: PARP inhibitors are maintenance options in advanced or recurrent carcinoma, particularly with BRCA mutations.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy is reserved for advanced invasive carcinoma, not an ovary-confined borderline tumor.

questions.stem: A 39-year-old woman has a 28-cm unilateral multiloculated ovarian mass removed. The cut surface shows numerous cysts separated by delicate septa and filled with thick, gelatinous material; the cysts are lined by columnar mucin-producing epithelium. Which of the following serum markers is most likely to be secreted by this tumor?

explanation.summary: Mucinous ovarian tumors secrete carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA).
explanation.whyCorrect: A very large, unilateral, multiloculated cyst filled with gelatinous mucin and lined by columnar mucinous epithelium is a mucinous tumor. Mucinous tumors secrete CEA, which can be used as a tumor marker.

whyWrongByChoice.A: CA-125 is elevated in many epithelial carcinomas, particularly advanced high-grade serous carcinoma, and is not the marker tied to mucinous tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Alpha-fetoprotein is produced by yolk sac tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Inhibin is secreted by granulosa cell tumors and other sex cord-stromal tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Estrogen is produced by theca cell and granulosa cell tumors.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old woman undergoes laparotomy for progressive abdominal distention and early intestinal obstruction. The peritoneal cavity contains massive gelatinous ascites with cystic epithelial implants studding the peritoneal surfaces and both ovaries. Which of the following is the most likely primary source of this process?

explanation.summary: Pseudomyxoma peritonei is now understood to arise mostly from an extra-ovarian source, usually the appendix.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mucinous ascites with cystic epithelial implants on peritoneal surfaces, adhesions, and ovarian involvement defines pseudomyxoma peritonei, which can cause intestinal obstruction and death. Although once attributed to primary ovarian mucinous neoplasms, it is now mostly attributed to an appendiceal primary.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ovarian mucinous neoplasms were historically blamed, but the ovaries are usually secondarily involved rather than the source.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The endometrium is not the described origin of pseudomyxoma peritonei.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The fallopian tube is the origin of high-grade serous carcinoma precursors, not mucinous peritoneal disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The bladder is not a described source of this mucinous process.

questions.stem: A healthy 48-year-old woman asks whether an annual blood test for CA-125 could screen her for ovarian cancer. She has no family history of malignancy. Which of the following best explains why CA-125 is not recommended for this purpose?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is elevated in many benign and non-ovarian conditions

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is undetectable until cancer becomes metastatic

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is produced only by germ cell tumors

choices.label: D
choices.text: It cannot be measured reliably in serum

choices.label: E
choices.text: It normalizes too quickly after tumor growth begins

explanation.summary: CA-125 has too many false positives to serve as a screening test.
explanation.whyCorrect: CA-125 is elevated in cancers of the endometrium, pancreas, breast, lung, and colon, and in benign conditions such as endometriosis, cirrhosis, peritonitis, pelvic inflammatory disease, and pancreatitis. This lack of specificity limits its use as a screening tool, although it is useful for follow-up after a firm diagnosis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: CA-125 is detectable in many epithelial ovarian carcinomas; the issue is specificity, not late detectability.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CA-125 is associated with epithelial ovarian carcinomas; yolk sac tumors produce alpha-fetoprotein.
whyWrongByChoice.D: CA-125 is measured in serum and used routinely to follow therapy response.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The marker is used to follow disease over time, so persistence is not the limitation.

questions.stem: A 41-year-old woman with a BRCA2 mutation undergoes risk-reducing bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. The pathologist pays particular attention to the fimbriated ends of the fallopian tubes. This examination is directed at finding the precursor lesion of which of the following tumors?

explanation.summary: High-grade serous carcinoma arises from serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma (STIC) in the fallopian tube fimbriae.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the type II pathway, intraepithelial carcinoma first develops in the fallopian tube epithelium (STIC) and progresses to high-grade serous carcinoma. This is the tumor type that dominates in BRCA mutation carriers, so the tubal fimbriae are scrutinized.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Low-grade serous carcinoma arises through the type I stepwise pathway from benign and borderline serous tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mucinous carcinoma develops through the type I pathway from cystadenoma and borderline tumors, not tubal lesions.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Endometrioid carcinoma is associated with endometriosis, not tubal intraepithelial lesions.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Brenner tumors are usually benign and are not linked to a tubal precursor.

questions.stem: A 47-year-old woman with a long history of surgically documented endometriosis develops a solid and cystic left ovarian mass with foci of hemorrhage. Histology shows an abundance of back-to-back malignant glands closely resembling endometrial tissue. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Malignant glands resembling endometrium arising in a patient with endometriosis indicate endometrioid carcinoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: Endometrioid tumors are histologically similar to endometrial tissue with a glandular appearance, and many show a close association with endometriosis, suggesting direct malignant transformation. The majority of endometrioid tumors are malignant.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Serous cystadenoma is a benign thin-walled cyst lined by ciliated fallopian tube-like epithelium.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mucinous borderline tumors show proliferative mucin-producing columnar epithelium, not endometrium-like glands.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Brenner tumors contain nests of urothelium-like epithelium and are usually benign.
whyWrongByChoice.E: High-grade serous carcinoma shows high-grade atypia and psammoma bodies and arises from tubal precursors, not endometriosis.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman has an ovarian mass excised incidentally during another pelvic operation. Microscopy shows well-circumscribed nests of epithelial cells resembling urothelium embedded in dense ovarian stroma. Which of the following best describes the expected clinical behavior of this tumor?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Usually recurs as gelatinous peritoneal implants

explanation.summary: Brenner (transitional cell) tumors contain urothelium-like epithelial nests and are usually benign.
explanation.whyCorrect: Nests of neoplastic epithelium resembling urinary tract epithelium within ovarian stroma define a transitional cell (Brenner) tumor. These tumors are usually benign.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Widespread peritoneal metastasis at diagnosis characterizes serous carcinoma, not Brenner tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gelatinous peritoneal implants describe pseudomyxoma peritonei, associated with mucinous processes of appendiceal origin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Alpha-fetoprotein is a marker of yolk sac tumors, which are germ cell tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Endometrioid and clear cell tumors, not Brenner tumors, can arise from endometriosis.

questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman with a strong family history of ovarian cancer asks what factors might lower her risk of developing the disease. Which of the following is associated with a decreased risk of ovarian cancer?

choices.label: E
choices.text: A high lifetime number of ovulatory cycles

explanation.summary: Oral contraceptive use, breast-feeding, and tubal ligation are protective, likely by reducing ovulatory cycles.
explanation.whyCorrect: Oral contraceptive use is protective against ovarian tumors, likely because it results in fewer lifetime ovulatory cycles. Breast-feeding and tubal ligation share this protective effect.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Nulliparity increases risk because it raises the lifetime number of ovulatory cycles.
whyWrongByChoice.B: BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations impair homologous recombination DNA repair and raise the risk of breast and ovarian cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ovarian cancer in a mother or sister increases the incidence 4- to 5-fold.
whyWrongByChoice.E: More ovulatory cycles increase, rather than decrease, ovarian cancer risk.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman has a 7-cm complex ovarian mass on ultrasound, and CT shows no disease outside the pelvis. A trainee proposes a percutaneous needle biopsy to obtain a tissue diagnosis before surgery. Which of the following is the best reason to avoid this approach?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Needle biopsy cannot obtain diagnostic epithelial cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: It may seed the peritoneal cavity with tumor cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Serum CA-125 alone confirms the diagnosis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most masses at this age are functional cysts

explanation.summary: Needle biopsy of an ovarian mass risks seeding the peritoneal cavity with malignant or mucous-secreting cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: Needle biopsies are not commonly performed for ovarian masses because of the possibility of seeding the peritoneal cavity with malignant or mucous-secreting cells. Tissue diagnosis is instead obtained by surgical removal of part or all of the ovary.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The concern is spread of tumor cells, not an inability to sample the lesion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tumor markers complement histology but do not replace a tissue diagnosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Radiology may suggest a diagnosis, but tissue confirmation is still generally required before definitive therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Functional cysts that resolve spontaneously are a consideration in reproductive-age patients, not a 58-year-old.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old woman with high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma undergoes staging. Based on the embryologic origin of the ovaries and their blood supply from the aorta, lymphatic spread of this tumor is most likely to involve which of the following lymph node groups?

explanation.summary: Ovarian cancer spreads via lymphatics to the para-aortic nodes, reflecting the ovaries' abdominal embryologic origin.
explanation.whyCorrect: The ovaries descend from the fetal abdomen and their blood supply arises from the aorta, so lymphatic invasion by ovarian cancer characteristically involves the para-aortic lymph nodes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Superficial inguinal nodes do not follow the ovarian vessels' aortic origin.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Axillary nodes drain the upper limb and breast, not the ovaries.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Popliteal nodes drain the lower leg and are unrelated to ovarian lymphatics.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Supraclavicular nodes are not the characteristic first site of ovarian lymphatic spread.

questions.stem: Ovarian neoplasms are encountered in up to 8% of females over a lifetime, and their behavior varies widely by cell of origin. Approximately what proportion of all ovarian tumors are benign?

explanation.summary: The majority of ovarian tumors, roughly 80%, are benign and occur mostly in females 20 to 45 years of age.
explanation.whyCorrect: About 80% of ovarian tumors are benign, occurring mostly in young females between 20 and 45 years of age. Borderline tumors occur at slightly older ages, and malignant tumors are more common between 45 and 65 years.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This substantially understates the benign fraction; malignant tumors are the minority of ovarian neoplasms.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Benign tumors far outnumber malignant ones; less than half is too low.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This is closer but still below the stated proportion of benign tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 95% is the share of ovarian malignancies arising from surface epithelium, not the benign fraction of all ovarian tumors.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman is evaluated for intermittent pelvic pressure. Transvaginal ultrasonography shows a 6-cm unilateral cystic adnexal mass that persists unchanged on repeat imaging 3 months later, and it is resected. Which of the following categories of ovarian neoplasm is most likely?

explanation.summary: Patient age is a useful guide to the etiology of an ovarian mass; benign epithelial tumors predominate in females of reproductive age.
explanation.whyCorrect: Benign epithelial tumors are most commonly found in females of reproductive age, and most ovarian tumors overall are benign, occurring between 20 and 45 years. A persistent unilateral cyst in a 34-year-old fits this pattern.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Germ cell tumors are most common in pre-pubertal females, that is, children and adolescents.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Epithelial ovarian malignancies are most often found in females who are postmenopausal.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sex cord-stromal tumors, like germ cell tumors, account for only about 5% of ovarian malignancies and are far less common in this setting.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The ovary can be a site of metastasis from other cancers, but this is not the most likely source of an isolated adnexal cyst in a healthy 34-year-old.

questions.stem: A 37-year-old woman whose mother died of ovarian cancer undergoes germline testing, which identifies a pathogenic BRCA1 variant. The protein encoded by this gene normally participates in which of the following cellular processes?

explanation.summary: BRCA1 and BRCA2 encode proteins involved in homologous recombination DNA repair.
explanation.whyCorrect: BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes encode proteins involved in homologous recombination DNA repair, and mutations in these genes are associated with a higher risk of breast and ovarian cancer. Loss of this repair pathway underlies homologous recombination deficiency, which also predicts response to PARP inhibitor maintenance therapy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Mismatch repair is not the function attributed to the BRCA genes in this lecture.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Nucleotide excision repair is a distinct pathway and is not the described BRCA function.
whyWrongByChoice.D: BRCA proteins are DNA repair proteins, not components of the mitotic spindle apparatus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Telomere maintenance is unrelated to the repair function of BRCA1 and BRCA2.

questions.stem: A 57-year-old woman reports 3 months of constipation, bloating, and vague lower abdominal discomfort. Colonoscopy and upper endoscopy are unremarkable, and she is ultimately found to have an ovarian neoplasm. Which of the following best explains why her tumor produced this symptom pattern?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ovarian tumors invade the gastric wall early in their course

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ovarian tumors produce a specific, recognizable clinical syndrome

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ovarian tumors are usually detected by screening before symptoms

choices.label: D
choices.text: The ovaries lie in the pelvis and lower abdomen beside the bowel

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ovarian tumors reach the colon first by lymphatic invasion

explanation.summary: The pelvic location of the ovaries explains the nonspecific GI symptoms that ovarian masses classically produce.
explanation.whyCorrect: The location of the ovaries determines the most common symptoms when symptoms are present. Because the ovaries sit in the pelvis and lower abdomen, patients often describe GI symptoms such as constipation, abdominal or pelvic pain, and bloating. Because these symptoms are shared by many disorders, gynecologic causes belong in the differential diagnosis of a female with GI complaints.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ovarian cancer spreads by direct extension in the pelvis and peritoneum rather than by early gastric wall invasion.
whyWrongByChoice.B: There is no clinical presentation specific to ovarian cancer; the symptoms are notoriously nonspecific.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ovarian tumors are often asymptomatic and found incidentally, but there is no effective screening test for them.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Lymphatic invasion characteristically involves the para-aortic nodes and does not explain early bowel symptoms.

questions.stem: A 46-year-old woman has a firm, palpable left adnexal mass discovered on routine pelvic examination. She is hemodynamically stable and has no acute symptoms. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial diagnostic study?

choices.label: A
choices.text: CT of the abdomen and pelvis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Percutaneous needle biopsy of the mass

explanation.summary: Pelvic ultrasonography is the usual first test for a suspected pelvic mass.
explanation.whyCorrect: For any patient with a suspected pelvic mass, a pelvic ultrasound is usually a good first test. It can detect ovarian tumors as well as ovarian cysts, tubo-ovarian abscesses, and other pelvic pathology.

whyWrongByChoice.A: CT is useful to extend the examination to the surrounding abdomen and gauge spread, but it follows rather than replaces the initial ultrasound.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Needle biopsies are avoided because of the possibility of seeding the peritoneal cavity with malignant or mucous-secreting cells.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tumor markers complement tissue histology and help follow disease, but they do not serve as the initial diagnostic study.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Surgery may ultimately be needed for tissue diagnosis, but imaging comes first in an otherwise stable patient.

questions.stem: A 59-year-old woman is found on transvaginal ultrasonography to have a 9-cm complex right adnexal mass with solid components, and there is moderate ascites. Which of the following studies is most useful to determine the degree of spread before she is taken to the operating room?

choices.label: C
choices.text: CT of the abdomen and pelvis

explanation.summary: CT extends the evaluation beyond the pelvis and defines the degree of spread when cancer is suspected.
explanation.whyCorrect: A computed tomographic scan is useful to extend the examination to the surrounding abdomen and can also determine the degree of spread if cancer is present. This matters because ovarian cancer spreads by direct extension throughout the peritoneum, with metastases possible in the GI tract, liver, and pleural cavity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ultrasonography characterizes the pelvic mass itself but does not adequately survey the abdomen for spread.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hysteroscopy examines the uterine cavity and does not assess peritoneal or abdominal disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: CEA is a marker secreted by mucinous tumors; markers follow disease but do not map anatomic extent.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Colonoscopy evaluates the colonic lumen and would not define the extent of peritoneal or abdominal tumor.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman has a 4-cm simple, thin-walled cystic structure in the right ovary discovered incidentally during ultrasonography performed for renal colic. She is asymptomatic and has regular menses. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

explanation.summary: In females of reproductive age, serial imaging often replaces surgical exploration because many ovarian masses are functional cysts that resolve.
explanation.whyCorrect: In females of reproductive age, regular radiologic studies may be used instead of surgical exploration, because many masses are from functional ovarian cysts and resolve without intervention. This patient is young, asymptomatic, and has a simple-appearing cyst.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Oophorectomy is reserved for masses that require tissue diagnosis, not a simple cyst likely to resolve on its own.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Needle biopsy risks seeding the peritoneal cavity with malignant or mucous-secreting cells and is not routinely performed.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy is the surgical approach to ovarian carcinoma, not to a probable functional cyst.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Chemotherapy is used for invasive carcinoma and has no role for an incidental simple cyst.

questions.stem: Which of the following tumor markers is secreted by granulosa cell tumors and other sex cord-stromal tumors and acts to reduce pituitary FSH secretion?

explanation.summary: Inhibin is a sex cord-stromal tumor marker that reduces pituitary FSH secretion.
explanation.whyCorrect: Inhibin is secreted by granulosa cell tumors and other sex cord-stromal tumors, and this hormone reduces pituitary FSH secretion. It can therefore be followed as a tumor marker in these patients.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Alpha-fetoprotein is produced by yolk sac tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Carcinoembryonic antigen is secreted by mucinous ovarian tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.D: CA-125 is elevated in many epithelial ovarian carcinomas, particularly advanced high-grade serous carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Estrogen is produced by theca cell and granulosa cell tumors but does not suppress FSH in the manner described.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman reports 8 months of deepening voice, increasing facial and chest hair, and secondary amenorrhea. Pelvic examination and ultrasonography reveal a 5-cm solid right ovarian mass. Which of the following ovarian tumors most characteristically produces the hormones responsible for her symptoms?

explanation.summary: Sertoli-Leydig tumors produce androgens, which cause virilizing symptoms.
explanation.whyCorrect: Some ovarian tumors secrete hormones that cause symptoms pointing toward a diagnosis. Androgens are produced by Sertoli-Leydig tumors, and androgen excess accounts for the deepening voice, hirsutism, and amenorrhea described here.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Granulosa cell tumors secrete estrogen and inhibin rather than androgens.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Yolk sac tumors are marked by alpha-fetoprotein production, not androgen secretion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Serous cystadenomas are benign cystic epithelial tumors and are not hormonally active.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Brenner tumors contain urothelium-like epithelial nests and are usually benign and nonfunctional.

questions.stem: A 14-year-old girl has a 6-week history of a rapidly enlarging pelvic mass and abdominal pain. Ultrasonography shows a large solid right ovarian mass, and serum alpha-fetoprotein is markedly elevated. Which of the following ovarian tumors is most likely?

explanation.summary: Alpha-fetoprotein is produced by yolk sac tumors, a germ cell tumor typical of pre-pubertal and adolescent patients.
explanation.whyCorrect: Alpha-fetoprotein is the marker produced by yolk sac tumors. Germ cell tumors are most commonly found in pre-pubertal females, that is, children and adolescents, which fits this patient's age.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Granulosa cell tumors secrete inhibin and estrogen, not alpha-fetoprotein.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Mucinous tumors secrete carcinoembryonic antigen and form large mucin-filled cysts.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Serous borderline tumors present in adult females at a mean age of about 45 years and are not alpha-fetoprotein producers.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Brenner tumors are usually benign epithelial tumors and are not associated with alpha-fetoprotein.

questions.stem: Approximately 95% of ovarian malignancies originate from which of the following?

explanation.summary: The vast majority of ovarian malignancies arise from the surface epithelium of the ovary.
explanation.whyCorrect: About 95% of ovarian malignancies originate from the surface epithelium, which arises from the simple cuboidal cell layer surrounding the ovaries that extends to the fallopian tubes. Surface epithelial tumors account for 90% to 95% of all ovarian neoplasms.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Germ cell tumors, together with sex cord-stromal tumors, make up only about 5% of ovarian cancers.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sex cord-stromal tumors are part of the same 5% minority, not the dominant group.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The ovaries can be sites of metastasis from other cancers, but this is not the origin of 95% of ovarian malignancies.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vascular origin is not one of the three main groups of ovarian tumors.

questions.stem: A 46-year-old woman undergoes oophorectomy for a cystic ovarian mass. Pathology shows an invasive low-grade serous carcinoma arising immediately adjacent to an area of serous borderline tumor, which in turn merges with a benign cystadenomatous lining. This tumor most likely developed through which of the following sequences?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Tubal intraepithelial carcinoma to invasive carcinoma

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cystadenoma to borderline tumor to invasive carcinoma

choices.label: C
choices.text: Endometriosis to atypical glands to invasive carcinoma

choices.label: E
choices.text: Appendiceal neoplasm to ovarian surface implants

explanation.summary: Type I epithelial tumors progress stepwise from benign cystadenoma through a borderline tumor to low-grade carcinoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: Type I epithelial tumors progress in a step-wise fashion from benign tumors such as cystadenoma, through borderline tumors, to low-grade serous, endometrioid, or mucinous carcinoma. Finding all three zones in one specimen is the morphologic signature of this pathway, and low-grade serous carcinoma typically arises in association with a serous borderline tumor.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This describes the type II pathway, in which serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma progresses to high-grade serous carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Endometriosis is the background for endometrioid and clear cell tumors, not for a serous cystadenoma-borderline sequence.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Urothelium-like nests define Brenner tumors, which are usually benign.
whyWrongByChoice.E: An appendiceal mucinous primary seeding the peritoneum describes pseudomyxoma peritonei, not this serous lesion.

questions.stem: A 43-year-old woman has an ovarian tumor showing increased epithelial proliferation with complex papillae and mild to moderate nuclear atypia. The pathologist classifies the lesion as borderline rather than carcinoma. Absence of which of the following features supports this classification?

explanation.summary: Borderline tumors are separated from carcinoma by the absence of stromal invasion.
explanation.whyCorrect: Borderline tumors are distinguished from malignant tumors by a lack of stromal invasion, while their increasing epithelial proliferation distinguishes them from benign tumors. Their clinical behavior is intermediate between benign and malignant tumors of the same type.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Borderline tumors may show mitoses, although the mitotic rate is low; their presence does not make a tumor malignant.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Nuclei in serous borderline tumors are uniform but mildly to moderately atypical, so some atypia is expected.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Serous borderline tumors are in fact more often bilateral than benign serous tumors, so laterality is not the criterion.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Psammoma bodies are a histologic feature of serous tumors generally and do not define invasion.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman has a 12-cm thin-walled ovarian cyst with a smooth, glistening external surface and a smooth inner surface removed by cystectomy. Histology shows a lining of ciliated pseudostratified cuboidal to columnar epithelium supported by spindle cell stroma. This lining most closely resembles the epithelium of which of the following structures?

explanation.summary: Serous cystadenomas are lined by ciliated epithelium resembling that of the fallopian tube.
explanation.whyCorrect: Serous cystadenomas of the ovary are thin-walled cysts lined by ciliated pseudostratified cuboidal or columnar epithelium resembling that lining the fallopian tube, supported by variable amounts of spindle cell stroma. These benign tumors range from 5 to 20 cm and are cured by surgical excision.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Endometrium-like glandular tissue characterizes endometrioid tumors, which are usually malignant.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Endocervical-type mucin-secreting columnar cells are not the described ciliated serous lining.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Urothelium-like epithelium characterizes transitional cell (Brenner) tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Colonic-type epithelium is not the lining described for serous cystadenoma.

questions.stem: Benign serous ovarian tumors involve both ovaries in up to 25% of cases. By comparison, approximately what proportion of mucinous ovarian tumors are bilateral?

explanation.summary: Only about 5% of mucinous ovarian tumors are bilateral, far fewer than serous tumors.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mucinous tumors differ from serous tumors in several ways: the ovarian surface is rarely involved, and only 5% of mucinous tumors are bilateral. They also tend to form much larger cystic masses filled with thick, gelatinous mucin.

whyWrongByChoice.B: 15% is the share of ovarian serous tumors that fall into the borderline group, not the bilaterality of mucinous tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Up to 25% bilaterality describes benign serous tumors, the comparison group given in the stem.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Half of mucinous tumors being bilateral markedly overstates the figure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Bilateral involvement in the great majority of cases is not characteristic of any ovarian tumor group described here.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman has a unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy for a serous borderline tumor, and staging shows no extraovarian disease. She asks about her long-term risk. Progression to invasive low-grade serous carcinoma occurs in up to approximately what percentage of such patients?

explanation.summary: The course of serous borderline tumors is indolent, but up to about 7% progress to invasive low-grade serous carcinoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: The clinical course for patients with serous borderline tumors is characteristically indolent and protracted; however, there is a significant risk of progression to invasive low-grade serous carcinoma, reported in up to 7% of females. This risk justifies continued follow-up even after complete resection.

whyWrongByChoice.B: 20% overstates the risk and misrepresents the indolent nature of these tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.C: About 30% to 40% of borderline serous tumors have extraovarian implants, but that is a different figure from progression to invasion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Half of borderline tumors progressing to carcinoma would be inconsistent with their protracted, indolent course.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A majority progressing to invasive carcinoma would make these tumors effectively malignant, which they are not.

questions.stem: During staging surgery for a serous borderline tumor, macroscopic nodules of similar-appearing epithelium are found on the peritoneal surfaces and within a pelvic lymph node. Determining which of the following features of these lesions is most important for planning further therapy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Whether the lesions contain psammoma bodies

choices.label: B
choices.text: Whether the lesions are invasive or noninvasive

choices.label: C
choices.text: Whether the lesions are unilateral or bilateral

choices.label: D
choices.text: Whether the lesions secrete carcinoembryonic antigen

choices.label: E
choices.text: Whether the lesions contain gelatinous mucin

explanation.summary: Extraovarian implants of serous borderline tumors are subclassified as invasive or noninvasive, and that distinction drives management.
explanation.whyCorrect: Approximately 30% to 40% of borderline serous tumors are associated with similar-appearing lesions in the pelvis and intra-abdominal sites, including lymph nodes; these are termed implants and are subclassified into noninvasive and invasive types. Initial staging surgery is required to determine the extent of disease and exclude invasive implants, because there is no indication for adjuvant chemotherapy or radiation when disease is confined to the ovary or limited to noninvasive implants.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Psammoma bodies are a general feature of serous tumors and do not determine whether adjuvant therapy is needed.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Laterality of the ovarian tumor does not classify extraovarian implants.
whyWrongByChoice.D: CEA is a marker of mucinous tumors and is not relevant to serous borderline implants.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Gelatinous mucin describes pseudomyxoma peritonei from a mucinous, usually appendiceal, source.

questions.stem: A 48-year-old woman has an invasive serous ovarian carcinoma that arose in association with a serous borderline tumor. The nuclei show only mild to moderate atypia, and sequencing identifies a KRAS mutation. Compared with high-grade serous carcinoma, this tumor is most likely to show which of the following?

explanation.summary: Low-grade serous carcinoma arises with borderline tumors, carries KRAS or BRAF mutations, and has longer survival than high-grade disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: Low-grade serous carcinoma typically arises in association with serous borderline tumors, occurs at a slightly younger age, is associated with KRAS or BRAF mutations, shows lower-grade cytologic atypia, and has longer survival. High-grade serous carcinoma has the opposite profile on each point.

whyWrongByChoice.A: TP53 mutations characterize high-grade serous carcinoma, including nearly all carcinomas in BRCA mutation carriers.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Arising from in situ lesions in the fallopian tube fimbriae is the hallmark of high-grade serous carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Higher-grade cytologic atypia is a feature of high-grade, not low-grade, serous carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: High-grade serous carcinoma occurs at a slightly older age than low-grade disease.

questions.stem: Histologic sections of an ovarian serous carcinoma show numerous spheres composed of concentric layers of calcium that stain dark blue-purple. These structures are also characteristic of which of the following tumors?

explanation.summary: Psammoma bodies are characteristic of serous ovarian carcinoma, meningioma, and papillary thyroid carcinoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: The structures described are psammoma bodies, spheres of varying sizes made of concentric layers of calcium. Besides serous ovarian tumors, they are characteristic of two other cancers: meningioma and papillary thyroid carcinoma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Follicular thyroid carcinoma is not among the tumors linked to psammoma bodies; the papillary subtype is.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hepatocellular carcinoma is not associated with psammoma bodies.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Renal cell carcinoma is not one of the psammoma body-associated tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Small cell lung carcinoma is not associated with these concentric calcifications.

questions.stem: A 64-year-old woman with high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma undergoes total hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and debulking of visible tumor. Which of the following is the most appropriate postoperative therapy?

explanation.summary: Serous ovarian carcinoma is treated with surgery followed by platinum-based chemotherapy, most commonly carboplatin plus paclitaxel.
explanation.whyCorrect: Serous ovarian carcinoma is primarily treated surgically with total hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and debulking of visible tumor, followed by platinum-based chemotherapy, most commonly carboplatin plus paclitaxel.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Radiation is not the standard adjuvant modality for serous ovarian carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Tamoxifen is not part of the described treatment of serous ovarian carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: CA-125 is useful for following disease after diagnosis, but observation alone is inadequate after debulking of an invasive carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Anti-angiogenic therapy such as bevacizumab may be added to treatment, but it is not given alone in place of chemotherapy.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman undergoes surgical staging and cytoreduction for an invasive mucinous ovarian carcinoma. Which of the following is an essential additional component of her management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Measurement of serum inhibin and estradiol

choices.label: C
choices.text: Adjuvant pelvic radiation to the tumor bed

explanation.summary: Mucinous ovarian carcinoma may represent metastasis from a GI primary, so a GI evaluation is essential.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because mucinous ovarian carcinomas may represent metastases from the gastrointestinal tract, evaluation for a GI primary tumor is an essential part of management. Unlike serous carcinoma, mucinous tumors are also less responsive to standard platinum-based chemotherapy, which is usually reserved for advanced-stage or metastatic disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Inhibin and estrogen are markers of sex cord-stromal tumors such as granulosa cell tumors, not mucinous carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.B: TP53 is the characteristic mutation of high-grade serous carcinoma; mucinous tumors consistently show KRAS alterations.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Radiation is not part of the described treatment of mucinous ovarian carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: PARP inhibitor maintenance applies to advanced or recurrent disease with BRCA mutations or homologous recombination deficiency.

questions.stem: A 49-year-old woman is found to have an ovarian endometrioid tumor. Which of the following best describes the expected behavior of most tumors of this histologic type?

explanation.summary: The majority of endometrioid ovarian tumors are malignant.
explanation.whyCorrect: The majority of endometrioid tumors are malignant, that is, endometrioid carcinoma. The benign and borderline variants are extremely rare.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Benign endometrioid tumors are extremely rare.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Borderline endometrioid tumors are also extremely rare.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fibromas and teratomas are the benign tumors noted to cause hormone-related symptoms, not endometrioid tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Functional ovarian cysts, not neoplasms, are the masses that resolve without intervention.

questions.stem: A 51-year-old woman with long-standing endometriosis is found to have an 18-cm cystic left ovarian mass. Histologic sections show solid sheets and tubules formed by large cells with abundant clear cytoplasm, intermixed with cells having solid pink cytoplasm. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Large cystic ovarian masses composed of clear cells forming sheets and tubes are clear cell carcinomas, which may arise from endometriosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Clear cell tumors are usually malignant surface epithelial tumors that may arise from endometriosis. They present as large cystic masses averaging more than 15 cm and are composed of large cells with abundant clear cytoplasm, although malignant cells may also have solid pink cytoplasm; the cells form solid sheets or tubes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Endometrioid carcinoma also associates with endometriosis but shows back-to-back malignant glands resembling endometrium rather than clear cells.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mucinous carcinoma forms multiloculated cysts filled with gelatinous mucin and lined by columnar mucinous epithelium.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Serous borderline tumors show branching papillae lined by ciliated cuboidal to columnar cells without stromal invasion.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Brenner tumors consist of nests of urothelium-like epithelium within ovarian stroma and are usually benign.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old woman newly diagnosed with ovarian carcinoma asks why this cancer causes so many deaths even though it is far less common than breast cancer. Which of the following best explains the disproportionate mortality of ovarian cancer?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Most tumors have spread beyond the ovary by diagnosis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ovarian tumors are uniformly resistant to chemotherapy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ovarian tumors spread preferentially to the brain

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ovarian carcinoma is more common than breast carcinoma

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ovarian tumors are not amenable to surgical resection

explanation.summary: Ovarian cancer kills disproportionately because it is usually advanced at the time of diagnosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because most ovarian cancers have spread beyond the ovary and fallopian tube by the time of diagnosis, they account for a disproportionate number of cancer deaths from gynecologic malignancies, and ovarian cancer is the most common cause of cancer death from gynecologic malignancy in the United States. Early direct extension produces minimal, nonspecific symptoms, so disease is usually found only after spread well beyond the pelvis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Serous carcinomas respond to platinum-based chemotherapy; mucinous carcinomas are the ones described as less responsive.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Spread is by direct extension through the peritoneum, lymphatics, and to the pleural cavity, not preferentially to the brain.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ovarian cancer incidence is 13 per 100,000 per year compared with 124 per 100,000 for breast cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Surgical resection with debulking is the mainstay of treatment for ovarian carcinoma.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman who has been postmenopausal for 6 years presents with new vaginal bleeding. Endometrial biopsy shows endometrial hyperplasia. Pelvic imaging reveals a solitary right adnexal mass, and serum inhibin is elevated. Histology of the resected mass shows sheets of tumor cells punctuated by small rosette-like structures surrounding eosinophilic basement membrane-type material. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Granulosa cell tumors overproduce estrogen, secrete inhibin, and show Call-Exner bodies on histology.
explanation.whyCorrect: Estrogen excess from a granulosa cell tumor drives endometrial hyperplasia and postmenopausal bleeding. Elevated inhibin, a peptide normally secreted by granulosa cells, supports the diagnosis, and the rosette-shaped structures around eosinophilic material are Call-Exner bodies, the characteristic histologic finding. Adult granulosa cell tumors occur predominantly in postmenopausal women.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Fibromas are not hormonally active, so they do not cause endometrial hyperplasia; they show spindle cells in a storiform pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Thecomas produce estrogen and can cause abnormal bleeding, but they are composed of plump vacuolated cells and are not associated with elevated inhibin or Call-Exner bodies.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sertoli-Leydig cell tumors secrete testosterone and cause virilization rather than estrogen-driven bleeding.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Dysgerminomas are germ cell tumors of adolescents with fried-egg cells and elevated LDH, not estrogenic tumors of postmenopausal women.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old woman presents with pelvic discomfort and increasing abdominal girth. Evaluation reveals a solitary ovarian mass, ascites, and a right pleural effusion. Serum CA-125 is elevated. The resected tumor is well-circumscribed with a smooth, homogeneous white cut surface, and histology shows spindle cells in a storiform arrangement. After removal of the tumor, the ascites and pleural effusion resolve. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Fibroma with ascites and pleural effusion that resolve after tumor removal defines Meigs syndrome.
explanation.whyCorrect: Meigs syndrome consists of a benign ovarian tumor, most commonly a fibroma, with ascites and pleural effusion that resolve when the tumor is removed. The white cut surface and storiform spindle cell histology are classic for fibroma. Fibromas can also elevate CA-125, which can falsely raise suspicion for ovarian carcinoma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The effusions resolving after excision of a benign-appearing, well-circumscribed spindle cell tumor indicates Meigs syndrome, not carcinoma, despite the elevated CA-125.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Thecomas have a solid yellow cut surface with plump vacuolated cells and are estrogenically active; they are not the classic Meigs syndrome tumor.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Granulosa cell tumors show Call-Exner bodies and secrete estrogen and inhibin rather than producing this benign spindle cell picture.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Krukenberg tumors are metastases, most commonly from gastric adenocarcinoma, and feature signet-ring cells, not storiform spindle cells.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman presents with 4 months of progressive deepening of her voice, new facial hair growth, and clitoral enlargement. Serum testosterone is markedly elevated. Imaging shows a discrete solid, yellow-tan right ovarian mass. Histology demonstrates well-formed tubules intermixed with polygonal cells. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Sertoli-Leydig cell tumors secrete testosterone and cause new, rapid virilization in females.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although testicular cell types are not normally found in the ovary, Sertoli-Leydig cell tumors rarely occur there, with peak incidence in the second and third decades. They secrete testosterone, producing rapid virilization. Histology of a well-differentiated tumor shows Sertoli tubules intermixed with Leydig cells, matching this specimen.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Granulosa cell tumors overproduce estrogen, causing bleeding or precocious puberty rather than virilization.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hyperthecosis causes virilization through diffuse luteinized stromal proliferation replacing ovarian tissue, not a discrete tubule-forming mass.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Thecomas are estrogen-producing benign tumors and would not raise testosterone or cause virilization.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Fibromas are hormonally inactive spindle cell tumors and do not cause virilization.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman undergoes pelvic imaging after a minor motor vehicle collision, which incidentally reveals a 7-cm solid and cystic left ovarian mass containing fat, hair, and calcifications. She is asymptomatic. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Conservative excision with examination of the opposite ovary

choices.label: C
choices.text: Neoadjuvant bleomycin, etoposide, and cisplatin chemotherapy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Radiation therapy directed at the pelvis and para-aortic nodes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Complete surgical staging with adjuvant combination chemotherapy

explanation.summary: Mature cystic teratomas are benign, and conservative excision is curative.
explanation.whyCorrect: A cystic and solid mass containing fat, hair, and calcifications in a reproductive-age woman is a mature cystic teratoma, the most common germ cell tumor. These are benign, and conservative excision is curative. Because teratomas can be bilateral, the opposite ovary requires examination and possible biopsy at the time of operation.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Removing the uterus and both adnexa is far more radical than needed for a benign lesion curable by conservative excision.
whyWrongByChoice.C: BEP chemotherapy is used for malignant germ cell tumors such as dysgerminoma, not for a benign mature teratoma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Radiation has no role in managing a benign mature cystic teratoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Staging with adjuvant chemotherapy is reserved for malignant tumors such as grade II-III immature teratomas, not mature teratomas.

questions.stem: A 41-year-old woman presents with palpitations, heat intolerance, tremor, and weight loss. TSH is suppressed and free T4 is elevated. The thyroid gland is normal on examination, but pelvic imaging reveals a right ovarian mass. Pathology of the resected mass shows a cystic teratoma composed predominantly of thyroid follicles. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Struma ovarii is a specialized teratoma containing thyroid tissue that can cause hyperthyroidism.
explanation.whyCorrect: Struma ovarii, comprising about 3% of all teratomas, is a specialized teratoma containing thyroid tissue. Functional thyroid tissue within the tumor can present with hyperthyroidism, explaining this patient's thyrotoxic symptoms despite a normal cervical thyroid gland.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Immature teratomas contain immature elements such as neuroepithelium forming rosettes and occur mostly in children and adolescents; they are not defined by thyroid tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Choriocarcinomas are trophoblastic tumors that secrete hCG; they do not contain thyroid follicles.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Granulosa cell tumors are estrogen-secreting stromal tumors and would not produce thyroid hormone.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Dysgerminomas show sheets of fried-egg cells with lymphocytic septa, not organized thyroid tissue.

questions.stem: A 17-year-old girl presents with pelvic fullness and is found to have a solid left ovarian mass. Serum lactate dehydrogenase is elevated. Histology shows sheets of tumor cells with round central nuclei and abundant clear cytoplasm, separated by strands of connective tissue filled with lymphocytes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Dysgerminoma shows fried-egg cells with lymphocyte-rich septa and elevated LDH in adolescents.
explanation.whyCorrect: Dysgerminomas are malignant germ cell tumors that most commonly present in adolescents and are associated with elevated serum LDH. The described cells with round central nuclei and abundant clear cytoplasm are the classic fried-egg appearance, and the connective tissue strands filled with lymphocytes complete the picture. The same tumor in the testis is called a seminoma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Yolk sac tumors are marked by elevated AFP and Schiller-Duval bodies, not fried-egg cells with elevated LDH.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Immature teratomas contain immature neuroepithelium, cartilage, or gut epithelium rather than uniform clear-cell sheets.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Choriocarcinoma is composed of trophoblastic tissue and produces markedly elevated hCG.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Granulosa cell tumors show Call-Exner bodies and secrete estrogen and inhibin; they occur predominantly in postmenopausal women.

questions.stem: A 9-year-old girl presents with abdominal pain and a rapidly growing pelvic mass involving a single ovary. Serum alpha-fetoprotein is markedly elevated. Histology shows blood vessels surrounded by tumor cells protruding into empty spaces. She undergoes surgery followed by cisplatin-based chemotherapy. Which of the following should be used to monitor for tumor recurrence?

explanation.summary: Yolk sac tumors secrete alpha-fetoprotein, which serves as the marker for monitoring response and recurrence.
explanation.whyCorrect: This child has a yolk sac tumor: a rapidly growing single-ovary mass in a young patient with elevated AFP and Schiller-Duval bodies on histology. The yolk sac is the first fetal organ to secrete alpha-fetoprotein, and serum AFP levels are used to monitor treatment response and recurrence after surgery and cisplatin-based chemotherapy.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Beta-hCG monitors choriocarcinoma, a trophoblastic tumor, not yolk sac tumor.
whyWrongByChoice.C: LDH is the marker followed in dysgerminoma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Inhibin is used to monitor granulosa cell tumor recurrence.
whyWrongByChoice.E: CA-125 is described with fibromas and immature teratomas in this lecture, not as the surveillance marker for yolk sac tumors.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old woman who has never been pregnant presents with headache and dyspnea. Serum hCG is markedly elevated, but transvaginal ultrasound shows no intrauterine or ectopic pregnancy and instead reveals a solid right ovarian mass. Imaging identifies lesions in the lung and brain. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Ovarian choriocarcinoma arises from unfertilized germ cells, secretes hCG, and metastasizes early to brain and lung.
explanation.whyCorrect: Choriocarcinoma is a rare, highly malignant tumor of trophoblastic tissue that produces hCG and shows rapid progression with early metastases to distant sites including brain and lung. In a patient who has never been pregnant, the tumor must have arisen from unfertilized germ cells in the ovary, distinguishing it from gestational choriocarcinoma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gestational choriocarcinoma is a malignant sequela of a pregnancy, typically molar; this patient has never been pregnant.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Dysgerminomas elevate LDH, not hCG, and metastasize mainly to peritoneum, bone, liver, lung, and regional nodes rather than presenting with marked hCG elevation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Yolk sac tumors secrete alpha-fetoprotein rather than hCG.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Immature teratomas present with elevated CA-125 with or without AFP and immature tissue elements, not marked hCG elevation.

questions.stem: A 14-year-old girl presents with abdominal distension and pain. Imaging shows a solid and cystic ovarian mass, and serum CA-125 is elevated. Resection reveals a heterogeneous tumor with hemorrhagic foci; histology shows abundant immature neuroepithelial elements forming rosettes, and the tumor is classified as grade III. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Conservative excision followed by surveillance alone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Surgery with staging followed by adjuvant chemotherapy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pelvic radiation therapy without further surgery

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hormonal therapy with serial serum marker monitoring

choices.label: E
choices.text: Observation with repeat imaging in six months

explanation.summary: Grade II and III immature teratomas require surgery, staging, and adjuvant chemotherapy.
explanation.whyCorrect: This adolescent has an immature teratoma, a tumor of children and adolescents containing immature elements, most commonly neuroepithelium, cartilage, or gut epithelium. Management is based on grade and stage: grade I tumors are treated with conservative excision and surveillance, but grade II and III tumors are treated with surgery, staging, and adjuvant chemotherapy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Excision with surveillance alone is appropriate only for grade I immature teratomas.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Radiation alone is not the described management for immature teratomas of any grade.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hormonal therapy is mentioned for recurrent granulosa cell tumors, not for immature teratomas.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Observation is inadequate for a grade III malignant tumor that requires adjuvant chemotherapy.

questions.stem: A 54-year-old woman with a history of gastric adenocarcinoma treated 2 years ago presents with pelvic pressure. Imaging reveals bilateral solid ovarian masses, each 7 cm, with nodular surface growth. Histology shows an infiltrative tumor with stromal desmoplasia and abundant signet-ring cells. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Krukenberg tumor is an ovarian metastasis, most commonly from gastric adenocarcinoma, with signet-ring cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bilateral involvement, size under 10 cm, surface involvement with nodular growth, an infiltrative pattern with stromal desmoplasia, a signet-ring cell component, and a known non-ovarian primary are all features favoring metastatic disease. With a gastric primary, this is a Krukenberg tumor, one of the most important metastatic ovarian tumors.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Granulosa cell tumors are primary estrogen-secreting stromal tumors with Call-Exner bodies, not signet-ring cells.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fibromas are unilateral benign spindle cell tumors with a storiform pattern, not bilateral infiltrative masses.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mature teratomas are cystic tumors containing hair, teeth, or other recognizable tissues from multiple embryonic layers.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Endometriomas are cystic structures formed by endometriosis on the ovary, not solid signet-ring cell tumors.

questions.stem: A pathologist is evaluating an 11-cm ovarian tumor and notes that tumors measuring 10-13 cm fall into an overlap zone that cannot be classified by size alone. Which of the following additional features would most strongly favor metastatic disease over a primary ovarian tumor?

explanation.summary: Bilateral involvement favors metastatic disease, while unilateral involvement and large size favor a primary ovarian tumor.
explanation.whyCorrect: Features favoring metastatic disease include bilateral involvement, size under 10 cm, surface or superficial cortical involvement, nodular growth, an infiltrative pattern with stromal desmoplasia, a signet-ring cell component, hilar or lymph-vascular invasion, and a known non-ovarian primary. None of these is pathognomonic, but bilaterality is the metastatic-favoring feature among the options.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Unilateral involvement favors a primary ovarian tumor.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tumors larger than 13 cm are more likely primary ovarian tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Absence of nodularity favors a primary ovarian tumor; nodular growth is the metastatic-favoring pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cyst formation is a feature shared by both primary and metastatic lesions, so it does not discriminate.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman presents with gradual coarsening of body hair and clitoral enlargement. Imaging shows mildly enlarged ovaries without a discrete mass. Pathology after oophorectomy demonstrates diffuse replacement of normal ovarian tissue by a proliferation of luteinized stromal cells. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Hyperthecosis is diffuse luteinized stromal proliferation with excess androgen production causing virilization.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hyperthecosis occurs when normal ovarian tissue is replaced by a proliferation of luteinized stromal cells, producing excess androgen. As with Sertoli-Leydig cell tumors, virilization such as body hair growth and clitoral enlargement can occur. The diffuse stromal process without a discrete tumor mass distinguishes it here; luteoma of pregnancy is a rare variant of this condition.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Sertoli-Leydig cell tumors also virilize but form a discrete mass containing Sertoli tubules and Leydig cells.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Thecomas are discrete estrogen-producing tumors associated with abnormal bleeding, not diffuse androgenic stromal change.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fibromas are hormonally inactive spindle cell tumors and would not cause virilization.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Granulosa cell tumors overproduce estrogen, causing bleeding or precocious puberty rather than virilization.

questions.stem: Within the ovarian stroma, one cell type converts cholesterol into androgens, and a second cell type converts those androgens into estradiol. A tumor arising from the cell type responsible for the second step would be expected to overproduce estrogen. Which of the following cell types performs that second conversion?

explanation.summary: Theca cells convert cholesterol into androgens, and granulosa cells convert those androgens into estradiol.
explanation.whyCorrect: The ovarian stroma contains three important cell types: fibroblasts, theca cells, and granulosa cells. Theca cells perform the first step by converting cholesterol into androgens, and granulosa cells complete the pathway by converting androgens into estradiol. This is why granulosa cell tumors are best known for overproducing estrogen.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Fibroblasts are the hormonally inactive stromal component and give rise to fibromas, which produce no hormone.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Theca cells carry out the first step, converting cholesterol into androgens rather than making estradiol.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Luteinized stromal cells are the proliferating cells of hyperthecosis and produce excess androgen, not estradiol.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sertoli cells are testicular cell types not normally found in the ovary; they appear only in Sertoli-Leydig cell tumors.

questions.stem: A 64-year-old woman presents with vaginal bleeding 12 years after menopause. Imaging shows a solitary 6-cm right ovarian mass. The resected tumor has a solid, yellow cut surface, and histology shows plump cells with pale grey to vacuolated cytoplasm. No Call-Exner bodies are identified, and serum inhibin is not elevated. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Thecomas are benign, estrogen-producing stromal tumors with a solid yellow cut surface and plump vacuolated cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: Thecomas typically occur in older adult females as solitary masses. Grossly, the tumor has a solid, yellow cut surface, and histologically it is composed of plump cells with pale grey to vacuolated cytoplasm. Because they are hormonally active and produce estrogen, thecomas can be associated with abnormal vaginal bleeding.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Fibromas are not hormonally active and would not cause postmenopausal bleeding; they are well-circumscribed with a smooth white cut surface and storiform spindle cells.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Granulosa cell tumors also produce estrogen, but they show Call-Exner bodies and elevated inhibin, both of which are explicitly absent here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sertoli-Leydig cell tumors secrete testosterone and produce virilization, and their histology shows Sertoli tubules with Leydig cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hyperthecosis is diffuse replacement of ovarian tissue by luteinized stromal cells producing excess androgen, not a discrete estrogenic mass.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old woman reports several months of a pulling sensation in her groin. Imaging shows a solitary 5-cm left ovarian mass, and biopsy shows a proliferation of bland spindle cells in a storiform arrangement consistent with a fibroma. Which of the following is considered adequate treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and debulking

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hormonal therapy with serial imaging surveillance

explanation.summary: Fibromas and thecomas behave in a benign fashion, and oophorectomy or salpingo-oophorectomy is adequate treatment.
explanation.whyCorrect: Both fibromas and thecomas are rare, benign stromal tumors that behave in a benign fashion. Removal of the ovary, or removal of the fallopian tube and ovary together, is considered adequate treatment; no adjuvant therapy is required.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Removing the uterus and both adnexa with debulking is reserved for advanced malignant disease, such as advanced-stage juvenile granulosa cell tumor.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Combination chemotherapy is used for malignant ovarian tumors; a fibroma behaves in a benign fashion after excision.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Radiation has no role in the treatment of a benign fibroma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fibromas are hormonally inactive, so hormonal therapy would have no effect, and the mass is already symptomatic.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old woman is diagnosed with an estrogen-producing ovarian tumor associated with elevated serum inhibin. She asks whether the hormone her tumor makes could cause a second cancer. Which of the following malignancies is she at greatest risk of developing as a consequence of this tumor's hormone secretion?

explanation.summary: Estrogen secreted by a granulosa cell tumor can drive endometrial hyperplasia and secondary endometrial cancer.
explanation.whyCorrect: Granulosa cell tumors overproduce estrogen, which causes endometrial hyperplasia and abnormal bleeding. Sustained secretion of these sex hormones can result in secondary carcinomas, with endometrial cancer being the one the lecture highlights.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gastric adenocarcinoma is a source of metastasis to the ovary (Krukenberg tumor), not a consequence of ovarian estrogen production.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cervical squamous cell carcinoma is not described as an estrogen-driven secondary malignancy of these tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Colon cancer commonly metastasizes to the ovary but is not caused by tumor estrogen secretion.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hepatocellular carcinoma has no described relationship to estrogen-secreting ovarian tumors.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman with a newly diagnosed ovarian tumor has an elevated serum level of a peptide normally secreted by granulosa cells. In healthy women, this peptide primarily serves which of the following functions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Regulation of pituitary secretion of follicle-stimulating hormone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conversion of cholesterol into androgens within theca cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Conversion of circulating androgens into estradiol

choices.label: D
choices.text: Maintenance of the placenta during early pregnancy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transport of fetal proteins analogous to albumin

explanation.summary: Inhibin, secreted by granulosa cells, helps regulate pituitary FSH secretion and serves as a granulosa cell tumor marker.
explanation.whyCorrect: Granulosa cell tumors are associated with elevated levels of inhibin, a peptide secreted by granulosa cells that plays a role in regulating pituitary secretion of follicle-stimulating hormone. Serum inhibin is therefore also used to monitor for tumor recurrence.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Converting cholesterol into androgens is the steroidogenic function of theca cells, not the action of a peptide hormone.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Conversion of androgens into estradiol is an enzymatic step performed by granulosa cells themselves, not a function of inhibin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Maintaining pregnancy is the natural function of hCG, the hormone produced by trophoblastic tissue and by choriocarcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The fetal albumin equivalent is alpha-fetoprotein, the marker of yolk sac tumors.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman undergoes salpingo-oophorectomy with complete staging for an adult granulosa cell tumor confined to one ovary. She asks how long she needs to be watched for the tumor returning. Which of the following statements about recurrence of this tumor is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Recurrence within the pelvis and abdomen may appear 10 to 20 years later

choices.label: B
choices.text: Recurrence essentially always declares itself within the first year

choices.label: C
choices.text: Recurrent disease is not amenable to further surgical therapy

choices.label: D
choices.text: These tumors are benign, so recurrence surveillance is unnecessary

choices.label: E
choices.text: Recurrence characteristically presents first as brain and lung metastases

explanation.summary: Malignant granulosa cell tumors pursue an indolent course, with pelvic and abdominal recurrences appearing 10 to 20 years later.
explanation.whyCorrect: Malignant granulosa cell tumors generally pursue an indolent course in which local recurrences are often amenable to surgical therapy. Recurrences within the pelvis and abdomen may appear 10 to 20 years after removal of the original tumor, so long-term follow-up with serum inhibin is used to monitor for recurrence.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Recurrence within the first year is the pattern described for dysgerminoma, not for granulosa cell tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Local recurrences are frequently amenable to surgery, and secondary cytoreductive surgery may benefit patients with recurrence.
whyWrongByChoice.D: All granulosa cell tumors are potentially malignant, with a 5% to 25% likelihood of recurrence or extension.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Rapid early metastasis to brain and lung characterizes choriocarcinoma, not granulosa cell tumor.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old woman undergoes surgery for an adult granulosa cell tumor. The pathologist notes that the histologic appearance does not reliably predict how the tumor will behave. Which of the following is the most important prognostic indicator in this tumor?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Patient age at the time of diagnosis

explanation.summary: For adult granulosa cell tumors, stage of disease is the most important prognostic indicator.
explanation.whyCorrect: It is difficult to predict the biologic behavior of granulosa cell tumors from histology, and the likelihood of malignant behavior ranges from 5% to 25%. For adult granulosa cell tumors, stage of the disease is the most important prognostic indicator, which is why salpingo-oophorectomy with complete staging is the initial therapeutic approach.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Call-Exner bodies are a diagnostic histologic feature, but histology does not reliably predict biologic behavior.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Tumor size is not described as the determinant of outcome in granulosa cell tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Estradiol level reflects hormonal activity and symptoms, not prognosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Age separates juvenile from adult forms and guides fertility-sparing surgery, but stage determines prognosis.

questions.stem: A 6-year-old girl is brought to the clinic because of breast development and vaginal bleeding that began 4 months ago. Examination reveals breast budding with pubic hair and a palpable lower abdominal mass. Serum inhibin is elevated, and imaging shows a unilateral solid ovarian mass. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: The juvenile form of granulosa cell tumor secretes estrogen and presents with precocious puberty and elevated inhibin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Granulosa cell tumors overproduce estrogen, and because sex hormones are secreted they may present with abnormal bleeding, tender breasts, or early puberty. Precocious puberty is the presentation of the juvenile form, which is distinguished from the adult form largely by patient age. Elevated inhibin supports a granulosa cell origin.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dysgerminomas most commonly present in adolescents with elevated LDH and are not hormonally active.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Yolk sac tumors present with abdominal pain and a rapidly growing pelvic mass with elevated AFP, not estrogen excess.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sertoli-Leydig cell tumors secrete testosterone and cause virilization, not breast development and bleeding.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mature cystic teratomas are usually benign, hormonally silent, and occur during reproductive age.

questions.stem: An 8-year-old girl is found to have a juvenile granulosa cell tumor confined to one ovary (stage IA). Her parents ask about preserving her future ability to have children. Which of the following is the preferred initial treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Combination chemotherapy in place of surgery

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pelvic radiation therapy followed by surveillance

choices.label: E
choices.text: Hormonal therapy with serial inhibin measurement
