explanation.summary: Juvenile granulosa cell tumors are treated with conservative unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and staging to preserve fertility.
explanation.whyCorrect: For juvenile granulosa cell tumors, conservative surgery consisting of unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy with complete staging is preferred, because most patients are young and have unilateral disease, and fertility can be preserved. Serum inhibin is then used to monitor for recurrence.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and debulking is reserved for advanced-stage disease, not stage IA.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Combination chemotherapy is added for disease beyond stage IA and for recurrences, not as a substitute for primary surgery.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Radiation is described only as an option in some instances of recurrent disease, not as initial therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hormonal therapy is used in recurrent disease; it does not treat a newly diagnosed localized tumor.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old woman undergoes salpingo-oophorectomy for a testosterone-secreting ovarian mass. Final pathology shows an intact, well-differentiated Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor with well-formed Sertoli tubules intermixed with Leydig cells, confined to the ovary without rupture. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

explanation.summary: Well-differentiated Sertoli-Leydig cell tumors are clinically benign, so salpingo-oophorectomy alone suffices.
explanation.whyCorrect: Prognosis of Sertoli-Leydig cell tumors depends on stage and degree of differentiation, and well-differentiated tumors are clinically benign. Therapy consists of salpingo-oophorectomy, with chemotherapy considered only for poorly differentiated tumors, ruptured intermediately differentiated tumors, and unusual variants. This intact, well-differentiated tumor needs no adjuvant treatment.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Chemotherapy is considered for poorly differentiated or ruptured intermediate-differentiation tumors, neither of which applies here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Removing the uterus and remaining ovary is unnecessary for a clinically benign unilateral tumor in a young woman.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Radiation is not part of the described treatment of Sertoli-Leydig cell tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Virilizing symptoms are driven by the tumor's testosterone production and are addressed by removing the tumor, not by adjuvant hormonal therapy.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman in the third trimester of pregnancy develops increasing coarse facial hair and deepening of her voice. Imaging shows enlarged ovaries without a discrete tumor, and biopsy shows a proliferation of luteinized stromal cells with excess androgen production. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Luteoma of pregnancy is a rare variation of hyperthecosis, with luteinized stromal proliferation and androgen excess.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hyperthecosis occurs when normal ovarian tissue is replaced by a proliferation of luteinized stromal cells with excess androgen production, and virilization such as body hair growth and clitoral enlargement can occur. Luteoma of pregnancy is described as a rare variation of this condition, fitting this pregnant patient with a diffuse luteinized stromal process rather than a discrete tumor.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Sertoli-Leydig cell tumors also virilize, but they form a discrete mass with Sertoli tubules and Leydig cells.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Thecomas produce estrogen and present as solitary masses in older adult females, typically with abnormal bleeding.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Granulosa cell tumors overproduce estrogen and would not cause virilization.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Endometriomas are cystic structures formed when endometriosis involves the ovary and are not hormonally active.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman with a 5-year history of cyclic pelvic pain is found to have a cystic left ovarian lesion. Pathology shows ectopic endometrial tissue forming the wall of the cyst. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Endometriomas are cystic ovarian structures that form when endometriosis involves the ovary.
explanation.whyCorrect: Endometriomas are cystic ovarian structures that occur when endometriosis, ectopic endometrial tissue, forms on the ovaries. Ectopic endometrial tissue lining an ovarian cyst is the defining finding.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Mature cystic teratomas contain tissues such as hair and teeth derived from at least two embryonic layers, not endometrial tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Thecomas are solid, yellow, estrogen-producing stromal tumors of older adult females.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Struma ovarii is a specialized teratoma containing thyroid tissue that may cause hyperthyroidism.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Fibromas are solid, white, hormonally inactive spindle cell tumors, not endometrial-lined cysts.

questions.stem: Mature cystic teratomas are well known for containing recognizable tissues such as hair and teeth. These tumors are composed of tissues derived from which of the following?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cells forming the yolk sac of the embryo

choices.label: E
choices.text: At least two of the three embryonic layers

explanation.summary: Teratomas contain a range of cells derived from at least two of the three embryonic layers.
explanation.whyCorrect: Teratomas are germ cell tumors well known for having a range of cells derived from at least two of the three embryonic layers: endoderm, mesoderm, and ectoderm. This is why they often contain recognizable tissues such as hair or teeth, which make them easy to identify.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Teratomas are not limited to ectoderm; tissues from multiple embryonic layers are present.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Trophoblastic tissue composes choriocarcinoma, which secretes hCG.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Luteinized stromal proliferation defines hyperthecosis, not a germ cell tumor.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Yolk sac-derived cells give rise to yolk sac tumors, which secrete alpha-fetoprotein.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman is found incidentally to have an asymptomatic 6-cm mature cystic teratoma of the right ovary. She asks what problems the tumor could cause if left in place. Which of the following is a recognized complication of this tumor?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ascites and pleural effusion that resolve after excision

choices.label: B
choices.text: Endometrial hyperplasia caused by estrogen excess

choices.label: E
choices.text: Signet-ring cell infiltration of the ovarian stroma

explanation.summary: Complications of mature cystic teratoma include torsion, rupture, infection, autoimmune hemolytic anemia, and virilization.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mature cystic teratomas are often asymptomatic and discovered incidentally, with abdominal pain the most common symptom when present. Recognized complications include torsion, acute or subacute rupture, infection, idiopathic autoimmune hemolytic anemia, and virilization.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ascites and pleural effusion that resolve after tumor removal define Meigs syndrome, associated with fibromas.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Estrogen-driven endometrial hyperplasia is caused by granulosa cell tumors and thecomas, not teratomas.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Marked and persistent hCG elevation characterizes choriocarcinoma, a trophoblastic tumor.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Signet-ring cells indicate metastatic disease, classically Krukenberg tumor from gastric adenocarcinoma.

questions.stem: A 12-year-old girl with abdominal distension undergoes resection of a solid and cystic ovarian mass. Pathology identifies a focus of immature neuroepithelium forming rosettes, and the tumor is designated grade I and confined to the ovary. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Surgery with complete staging plus adjuvant chemotherapy

explanation.summary: Grade I immature teratomas are treated with conservative excision followed by surveillance.
explanation.whyCorrect: Management of immature teratomas is based largely on tumor grade and stage at presentation. Grade I tumors are treated with conservative excision followed by surveillance, whereas grade II and III tumors require surgery, staging, and adjuvant chemotherapy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Radical surgery is not indicated for a grade I tumor in a child and would eliminate future fertility.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Staging with adjuvant chemotherapy is reserved for grade II and III immature teratomas.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Radiation is not part of the described management of immature teratomas.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Chemotherapy alone is not used, and a grade I tumor does not require chemotherapy at all.

questions.stem: A pathologist reviewing an ovarian teratoma identifies an immature tissue component. Which of the following best describes the frequency of this finding among ovarian teratomas and the group in which such tumors most often occur?

choices.label: A
choices.text: About 3%; most often in children and adolescents

choices.label: B
choices.text: About 3%; most often in postmenopausal women

choices.label: C
choices.text: About 30%; most often in children and adolescents

choices.label: D
choices.text: About 30%; most often in the third and fourth decades

choices.label: E
choices.text: About 50%; most often in the third and fourth decades

explanation.summary: Roughly 3% of ovarian teratomas have an immature component, and these occur more frequently in children and adolescents.
explanation.whyCorrect: Approximately 3% of ovarian teratomas feature an immature tissue component. Known as immature teratomas, these tumors occur more frequently in children and adolescents and present with abdominal distension and/or pain, usually with elevated CA-125 with or without elevated AFP.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The age association is with children and adolescents; postmenopausal predominance describes adult granulosa cell tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The proportion with immature elements is about 3%, not 30%.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Both figures are wrong: the frequency is about 3%, and the third and fourth decades are when mature cystic teratomas typically occur.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Half of all teratomas are not immature, and this age range corresponds to mature cystic teratomas.

questions.stem: A 16-year-old girl has a malignant ovarian germ cell tumor arising from primordial germ cells, with sheets of clear cells with round central nuclei interlaced by lymphocyte-filled connective tissue strands and an elevated serum LDH. The histologically equivalent tumor arising in the testis is known as which of the following?

explanation.summary: The testicular counterpart of an ovarian dysgerminoma is a seminoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: Dysgerminomas are malignant germ cell tumors originating from primordial germ cells destined to become gametes. They show a fried-egg appearance with round central nuclei and abundant clear cytoplasm, forming sheets interlaced with lymphocyte-filled connective tissue strands, and are associated with elevated LDH. This tumor in the testis is called a seminoma.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Sertoli cell elements appear in Sertoli-Leydig cell tumors, which are hormonally active sex cord stromal tumors, not the counterpart of dysgerminoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Yolk sac tumors have Schiller-Duval bodies and secrete AFP; they are a distinct germ cell tumor in either gonad.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Choriocarcinoma is composed of trophoblastic tissue and secretes hCG.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Teratomas contain tissues from at least two embryonic layers and are not composed of uniform clear-cell sheets.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old woman is diagnosed with a dysgerminoma confined to one ovary (stage IA), the stage at which roughly two-thirds of these tumors present. She asks about her chance of being alive in 5 years. Which of the following approximate 5-year survival rates is most accurate for her stage?

explanation.summary: Dysgerminoma 5-year survival is 75%-90% overall and about 90% for stage IA disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: Overall 5-year survival of dysgerminoma is 75% to 90% and is highly dependent on stage. It is approximately 90% for patients with stage IA disease, which accounts for about two-thirds of all cases, compared with 63% for patients with extraovarian disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This is far below the reported survival for any stage of dysgerminoma.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Even patients with extraovarian spread do better than 50% at 5 years.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 63% is the survival figure for patients with extraovarian disease, not stage IA.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Survival for stage IA disease is approximately 90%, not near universal.

questions.stem: A 20-year-old woman undergoes unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy with surgical staging for a dysgerminoma, with preservation of the grossly normal contralateral ovary. She is then referred for multiagent chemotherapy. Which of the following regimens is most commonly used in this setting?

explanation.summary: Dysgerminoma is treated with fertility-sparing surgery followed by multiagent chemotherapy, most commonly BEP.
explanation.whyCorrect: Primary treatment of dysgerminoma typically consists of unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy with surgical staging and preservation of a grossly normal contralateral ovary, followed by multiagent chemotherapy, most commonly BEP: bleomycin, etoposide, and cisplatin. Imaging and serum LDH are used to monitor for recurrence.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This combination is not the regimen described for dysgerminoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This combination is not used for ovarian germ cell tumors as described in this lecture.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This is not the regimen described for dysgerminoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This combination is not the regimen specified for dysgerminoma, which is treated with BEP.

questions.stem: A pathology report on a malignant ovarian germ cell tumor from a 12-year-old girl notes the presence of Schiller-Duval bodies. Which of the following best describes this histologic structure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A blood vessel surrounded by tumor cells, often protruding into an empty space

choices.label: B
choices.text: A small follicle-like rosette surrounding eosinophilic basement membrane-type material

choices.label: C
choices.text: A cell with round central nuclei and abundant clear cytoplasm in sheets

choices.label: D
choices.text: A proliferation of spindle cells in a woven, storiform arrangement

choices.label: E
choices.text: A cell with a nucleus displaced to the periphery by intracytoplasmic mucin

explanation.summary: Schiller-Duval bodies are blood vessels surrounded by tumor cells and are characteristic of yolk sac tumors.
explanation.whyCorrect: Yolk sac tumors are characterized histologically by Schiller-Duval bodies, which are blood vessels surrounded by tumor cells that often protrude into an empty space. These tumors arise from the cells that form the yolk sac of the embryo and secrete alpha-fetoprotein.

whyWrongByChoice.B: This describes Call-Exner bodies, the characteristic finding in granulosa cell tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This describes the fried-egg appearance of dysgerminoma cells.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This describes the storiform spindle cell proliferation of an ovarian fibroma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This describes a signet-ring cell, a feature of metastatic disease such as Krukenberg tumor.

questions.stem: The tumor marker used to follow patients with yolk sac tumors is a substance normally produced early in fetal development. Which of the following best describes this substance?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A peptide that helps regulate pituitary FSH secretion

choices.label: B
choices.text: A glycoprotein produced by trophoblastic tissue to maintain pregnancy

choices.label: C
choices.text: The fetal equivalent of albumin, first secreted by the yolk sac

choices.label: D
choices.text: A steroid formed when granulosa cells convert androgens

choices.label: E
choices.text: An enzyme released into serum with high tumor cell turnover

explanation.summary: Alpha-fetoprotein, the yolk sac tumor marker, is the fetal equivalent of albumin and is the yolk sac's first secreted hormone.
explanation.whyCorrect: The yolk sac is the first fetal organ to secrete alpha-fetoprotein, which is the equivalent of albumin for the fetus. Because yolk sac tumors derive from these cells, AFP serves as their tumor marker and is used to monitor response to therapy and detect recurrence.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This describes inhibin, the marker of granulosa cell tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This describes hCG, produced by trophoblastic tissue and by choriocarcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This describes estradiol, the product of granulosa cell aromatization of androgens.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This describes lactate dehydrogenase, the marker associated with dysgerminoma.

questions.stem: A 21-year-old nulligravid woman is diagnosed with an ovarian choriocarcinoma arising from unfertilized germ cells, with a markedly elevated serum hCG and pulmonary lesions. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Surgical resection alone with serial hCG measurement

choices.label: D
choices.text: Surgical resection followed by multiagent chemotherapy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pelvic radiation followed by hormonal therapy

explanation.summary: Choriocarcinoma is treated with surgical resection followed by multiagent chemotherapy, with beta-hCG used to follow response.
explanation.whyCorrect: Choriocarcinoma is an aggressive neoplasm showing rapid progression and early metastases to distant sites including brain and lung. Treatment includes surgical resection followed by multiagent chemotherapy, and beta-hCG levels are used to evaluate treatment response and detect recurrences.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Conservative excision with surveillance is appropriate for benign mature teratomas, not a highly malignant metastatic tumor.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Surgery alone is inadequate for a tumor with distant metastases; chemotherapy is required.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Treatment includes surgical resection in addition to chemotherapy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Radiation and hormonal therapy are not the described treatment for choriocarcinoma.

questions.stem: A 57-year-old woman is found to have bilateral ovarian masses that on biopsy are consistent with metastatic adenocarcinoma. Which of the following primary cancers is the most common source of metastasis to the ovary?

explanation.summary: Colon cancer is the most common primary that metastasizes to the ovary, followed by breast, stomach, and melanoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: Numerous tumors metastasize to the ovary, with colon cancer being the most common, along with breast, stomach, and skin (melanoma). Gastric adenocarcinoma is the classic source of the Krukenberg tumor, but colon is the most frequent primary overall.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Pancreatic cancer is not among the common primaries that spread to the ovary in this lecture.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Renal cell carcinoma is not listed among the common sources of ovarian metastasis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lung cancer is not among the listed common primaries metastasizing to the ovary.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Osteosarcoma is not a described source of ovarian metastasis.

questions.stem: A pathologist is trying to determine whether an ovarian tumor is a primary ovarian neoplasm or a metastasis. Which of the following features is shared by primary and metastatic ovarian lesions and therefore does not help distinguish between them?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Hilar involvement or lymph-vascular space invasion

explanation.summary: Necrosis, cyst formation, low-grade areas, and stromal luteinization occur in both primary and metastatic ovarian lesions.
explanation.whyCorrect: Features shared by primary and metastatic ovarian lesions include cyst formation, necrosis, low-grade areas suggesting a primary benign or borderline lesion, and stromal luteinization. Because necrosis appears in both columns, its presence carries no discriminating value, and no single feature is pathognomonic.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A signet-ring cell component favors metastatic disease, classically from gastric adenocarcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Nodular growth favors metastasis; absence of nodularity favors a primary ovarian tumor.
whyWrongByChoice.D: An infiltrative growth pattern with stromal desmoplasia is listed as a feature of metastatic disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hilar involvement or lymph-vascular space invasion favors metastatic disease.
